definition_zh: 帝国；疆域；庞大的企业集团
definition_en: a group of countries ruled by one sovereign; the territory so ruled; a large business group
core_image: 一张地图被同一条边界从海岸连到山脉
scene: 地图上一块块颜色被同一条边界连起来，向远方延伸。 The empire stretched from the sea to the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里 empire 是「帝国疆域」（第 01 个义项：由一个君主统治的多个地区）；句意是这个帝国从海边一直延伸到山区。

pos.zh: 名词：帝国；疆域；企业帝国

collocations.zh: 建立帝国；建立商业版图

derivatives.zh: 同词族的核心名词，义为「皇帝」，即帝国的统治者
由拉丁词根 imperium 加 -ial 构成，义为「帝国的；皇帝的」
由 imperial 加 -ism 构成，义为「帝国主义」

senses.title: A group of lands under one ruler
senses.definition: a group of countries or peoples ruled by a single sovereign
senses.definitionCN: 由一个君主统治的一组国家或民族
senses.example: The empire stretched from the sea to the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国从海边一直延伸到山区。
senses.why: The Latin source means command, so an empire is the whole territory where one command is obeyed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「命令」，所以帝国就是整套「同一条命令被服从」的疆域。

senses.title: The territory itself
senses.definition: the land and peoples considered as one domain
senses.definitionCN: 被看作一个整体的土地与人民
senses.example: Trade routes crossed the empire in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 商路四通八达地穿过帝国疆域。
senses.why: Command and the land that receives it are named together, so empire also means the map rather than the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 命令与接受命令的土地被一起命名，所以 empire 也指那张地图，而不是统治者本人。

senses.title: A large business group
senses.definition: a very large group of companies controlled by one person or organization
senses.definitionCN: 由一个人或组织控制的庞大公司群
senses.example: He built a media empire from a single newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他从一家报纸起家，打造了一个媒体帝国。
senses.why: A market can be ruled like a territory, so the word for political command extends to commercial dominance.
senses.whyCN: 市场可以像疆域一样被统治，于是这个表示政治统治的词扩展到了商业版图。

senses.title: Supreme authority, in older use
senses.definition: supreme command or dominion, an older abstract sense
senses.definitionCN: 最高的统治权或支配权，是较旧的抽象义项
senses.example: The old chronicle speaks of the empire of reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史谈到理性的统治。
senses.why: Before it named a place, imperium named the power itself, and empire can still mean dominion in formal or literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 在指一片土地之前，imperium 指的是权力本身，所以 empire 在正式或文学语境中仍可表示支配权。

intro.en: Empire comes from Latin imperium, the power to command, and only later names the land under that power.
intro.cn: empire 来自拉丁语 imperium（命令之权），后来才指受这种权力支配的土地。

items.en: The verb meant to command or give orders.
items.cn: 这个动词意为命令、发号施令。

items.en: The noun named supreme command and the authority behind it.
items.cn: 这个名词指最高指挥权及其背后的权威。

items.en: Empire carried the sense of rule and realm into French.
items.cn: empire 把统治与疆域的含义带入法语。

items.en: English empire first named imperial rule, then the ruled lands.
items.cn: 中古英语 empire 先指帝国统治，后指被统治的土地。

items.en: The word extended to business groups that rule a market.
items.cn: 现代英语又把它扩展到统治市场的商业集团。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the imperial family; the near-meaning group separates kingdom, realm and dominion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着帝国词族展开；近义组区分王国、领域与支配权。

entries.definition: The ruler who commands an empire.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「皇帝」，即统治帝国的人。

entries.definition: Relating to an empire or emperor.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「帝国的、皇帝的」。

entries.definition: The policy of extending an empire's power.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「帝国主义」。

entries.definition: A country ruled by a king or queen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「王国」，通常小于帝国。

entries.definition: A kingdom or a field of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「王国、领域」，可用于比喻。

entries.definition: Sovereign control or the territory controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支配权、领地」，对应本词的旧义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie empire to command, then let the commanded land become a map and later a market.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 empire 与「命令」绑在一起，再让受命令的土地变成地图，最后变成市场。

normal.en: Imperium means command, and an empire is where it is obeyed.
normal.cn: imperium 意为命令，帝国就是命令被服从的地方。

normal.en: An emperor rules an empire.
normal.cn: 皇帝统治帝国。

normal.en: The British Empire once covered many lands.
normal.cn: 大英帝国曾覆盖许多土地。

normal.en: A media empire rules screens instead of provinces.
normal.cn: 媒体帝国统治的是屏幕而不是省份。

normal.en: Imperial is the adjective of the same root.
normal.cn: imperial 是同根形容词。

abstract.en: Picture one border line swallowing many coloured regions.
abstract.cn: 想象一条边界线把许多彩色区域吞并进来。

abstract.en: The word starts as a command and ends as a map.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一道命令开始，最后变成一张地图。

abstract.en: Empire is authority drawn at scale.
abstract.cn: empire 就是被放大画出来的权威。

examples.en: The empire stretched from the sea to the mountains.
examples.cn: 这个帝国从海边一直延伸到山区。

examples.en: Trade routes crossed the empire in every direction.
examples.cn: 商路四通八达地穿过帝国疆域。

examples.en: He built a media empire from a single newspaper.
examples.cn: 他从一家报纸起家，打造了一个媒体帝国。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安派尔」——一人发令，整片地图都归他管

root: 经古法语 empire 来自拉丁语 imperium（统治权、帝国），其动词 imperare 由 in-（在上）加 parare（安排、命令）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Empire is a command obeyed across many lands, then the land itself, then a business domain, and in older use the authority itself.
sensesIntro.cn: empire 先是被多地服从的命令，再是那片土地，再是商业版图，较旧时还指权威本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one borderline joining coasts and mountains into a single map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界把海岸与山脉连成同一张地图。

branches.en: THE POLITY: many peoples under one ruler.
branches.cn: 政体线：多个民族受一个君主统治。

branches.en: THE MAP: the land seen as one domain.
branches.cn: 地图线：把土地看成一个整体领域。

branches.en: THE MARKET: companies ruled like provinces.
branches.cn: 市场线：公司像省份一样被统治。

branches.en: THE POWER: dominion as an abstract force.
branches.cn: 权力线：作为抽象力量的支配权。

branches.en: ONE SHAPE: polity, map and market share a border.
branches.cn: 同一形状：政体、地图与市场共享一条边界。

intro.en: Empire is a French borrowing from Latin imperium, so its endings are historical rather than productive.
intro.cn: empire 是经法语借入的拉丁语词，其词尾属于历史沉积而非能产词缀。

latinIntro.en: Imperare, imperium and imperator are recorded Latin forms of command and rule.
latinIntro.cn: imperare、imperium 与 imperator 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，表示命令与统治。

items.example: It is the base of imperare.

definition_zh: 居民；住户；住院医生；居住的
definition_en: a person who lives in a place, or living in a place
core_image: 清晨的街区，每扇门后都走出一位熟悉的面孔
scene: 每到周末，这条街的居民会把旧家具搬到人行道上出售。 Every weekend, the residents of this street put old furniture out on the pavement to sell.
sceneCN: 这里 resident 是「居民」（第 1 个义项：在某地居住的人）；句意：每到周末，这条街的居民会把旧家具搬到人行道上出售。

senses.title: A person who lives in a place
senses.definition: someone who lives in a particular house, street, or town
senses.definitionCN: 住在某栋房子、某条街或某个城镇的人
senses.example: The residents of the street meet every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街的居民每年春天聚会。
senses.why: The -ent ending names the person who carries out the action of residing.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ent 指执行「居住」这一动作的人。

senses.title: A doctor in hospital training
senses.definition: a doctor who has finished medical school and is training in a hospital
senses.definitionCN: 医学院毕业后在医院接受培训的医生
senses.example: She is a resident doctor at the city hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她是市医院的住院医生。
senses.why: The doctor lives at the hospital during training, so the residing word fits the role.
senses.whyCN: 这类医生在培训期间住在医院，因此「居住」这个词也适用于这一身份。

senses.title: Living in a place
senses.definition: living permanently in a particular place, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 长期住在某处，用于名词前
senses.example: A resident cat sleeps by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 一只常驻的猫睡在炉火旁。
senses.why: The adjective describes whatever stays in place rather than visiting.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述长期待在那里而非临时来访的人或动物。

intro.en: Resident comes from Latin residens, dwelling, the present participle of residere, to remain behind.
intro.cn: resident 来自拉丁语 residens（居住的），是 residere（留下）的现在分词。

items.en: Sedere means to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Residere means to remain behind or dwell.
items.cn: residere 意为留下、居住。

items.en: Residens means dwelling or remaining.
items.cn: residens 意为居住的、留下的。

items.en: Resident means dwelling in a place.
items.cn: resident 意为在某地居住的。

items.en: English resident names a person who lives in a place.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，英语 resident 指在某地居住的人。

items.en: Modern English adds the medical trainee sense.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「住院医生」这一义项。

note.en: Resident is the person noun of reside, and it sits near its family and near words for inhabitants.
note.cn: resident 是 reside 的人物名词，与自身词族以及表示居民的问相邻。

entries.definition: a home
entries.definitionCN: 住宅

entries.definition: to live in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居住

entries.definition: made up of homes
entries.definitionCN: 住宅的

entries.definition: a person or animal living in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居民；栖息动物

entries.definition: a legally recognized member of a country
entries.definitionCN: 公民

entries.definition: a person who lives in or uses a place
entries.definitionCN: 居住者；占用者

normalIntro.en: Resident is the person who resides: the one who lives there.
normalIntro.cn: resident 就是 reside 的人：住在那里的人。

normal.en: Add -ent to reside and you get the person.
normal.cn: 在 reside 后加 -ent，就得到那个人。

normal.en: Local resident is the usual newspaper phrase.
normal.cn: local resident 是新闻中常用的说法。

normal.en: A resident doctor lives at the hospital during training.
normal.cn: 住院医生在培训期间住在医院。

normal.en: Resident can also be an adjective: a resident cat.
normal.cn: resident 也可作形容词：a resident cat。

normal.en: Compare inhabitant: inhabitant is more formal and less common.
normal.cn: 对比 inhabitant：inhabitant 更正式，也更少用。

abstract.en: Picture a street where every door has a familiar face.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，每扇门后都是熟悉的面孔。

abstract.en: Imagine a doctor's coat hanging in a hospital room at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里医院房间里挂着一件白大褂。

abstract.en: Think of a cat that has slept by the same fire for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫在同一炉火旁睡了多年。

examples.en: The residents of the street meet every spring.
examples.cn: 这条街的居民每年春天聚会。

examples.en: She is a resident doctor at the city hospital.
examples.cn: 她是市医院的住院医生。

examples.en: A resident cat sleeps by the fire.
examples.cn: 一只常驻的猫睡在炉火旁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「reside + ent」——居住在那里的那个人，就是居民；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）→ residere（留下、居住）→ residens（居住的）→ 古法语 resident → 现代英语 resident。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the person who lives in a place, then a doctor who lives at a hospital during training, and can also describe anyone or anything staying in place.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指在某地居住的人，再指培训期间住在医院的医生，也可描述任何长期待在某处的人或物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar face stepping out of the same door each morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天清晨从同一扇门走出的熟悉面孔。

branches.en: A person living in a place is the main sense.
branches.cn: 在某地居住的人，是主要义项。

branches.en: The medical resident lives at the hospital while training.
branches.cn: 住院医生在培训期间住在医院。

branches.en: The adjective describes what stays rather than visits.
branches.cn: 形容词描述长期留下而非来访者。

branches.en: A person and an animal can both be resident somewhere.
branches.cn: 人与动物都可以是某地的常驻者。

branches.en: Both senses depend on living in a particular place.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「住在特定地方」。

intro.en: Resident is an English -ent noun and adjective built on the Latin verb residere.
intro.cn: resident 是建立在拉丁动词 residere 上的英语 -ent 名词兼形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit, residere means to remain, and residens means dwelling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，residere 意为留下，residens 意为居住的。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of remaining.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或动作的词尾

definition_zh: 智力的；知识分子的；n. 知识分子
definition_en: relating to thinking and understanding, or a person who lives by ideas and study
core_image: 书桌上一摞书、一叠写满的字纸，窗外的声音都被关在玻璃外
scene: 书房里的人整晚没离开过椅子，桌上摊着好几本书和批注。 Her intellectual curiosity took her from farming villages to a research library.
sceneCN: 这里 intellectual 是「智力的、求知方面的」（第 1 个义项：与思考理解有关），句意为求知的好奇心把她从农村带到研究图书馆。画面里的物件：摊开的书、批注笔、窗玻璃。

pos.zh: 形容词：智力的；脑力的；有才智的

derivatives.zh: 由本词的词干构成，义为「智力；才智」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在智力上」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「智力；情报」
由同一词干构成，义为「可理解的」

senses.title: Of thinking and learning
senses.definition: concerned with the ability to think, reason, and understand rather than with the body
senses.definitionCN: 关乎思考、推理与理解的能力，而非身体
senses.example: Chess is an intellectual game played mostly in silence.
senses.exampleCN: 国际象棋是一种几乎在静默中进行的智力游戏。
senses.why: Latin intellegere means to pick out and understand; -ual marks a quality.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intellegere 意为「辨出并理解」，-ual 标出性质。

senses.title: Enjoying ideas
senses.definition: enjoying serious reading, discussion, and ideas for their own sake
senses.definitionCN: 以严肃的阅读、讨论与思考本身为乐
senses.example: Their conversations were intellectual and went on until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的谈话富于思考，一直持续到天亮。
senses.why: By the eighteenth century the adjective described a lively taste for debate and learning.
senses.whyCN: 到十八世纪，这个形容词用来形容对辩论与学问的浓厚兴致。

senses.title: A person of ideas
senses.definition: a person, especially a well-known one, who writes or speaks seriously about ideas
senses.definitionCN: 尤指知名的人，认真写作或谈论思想的人
senses.example: The newspaper invited several intellectuals to argue about education.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸邀请了几位知识分子讨论教育问题。
senses.why: The noun use spread in the late nineteenth century, often with a faint hint of suspicion.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法在十九世纪末流行开来，往往略带一点怀疑的意味。

intro.en: Intellectual goes back to Latin intellegere, whose heart is legere "to choose, to read".
intro.cn: intellectual 上溯到拉丁语 intellegere，其核心是 legere「挑选、读」。

items.en: Legere meant to gather or pick, and so to read; inter- means "between, among".
items.cn: legere 意为「采集、挑」，因而「阅读」；inter- 意为「在……之间」。

items.en: Intellegere thus means to pick out the sense among things, that is, to understand.
items.cn: 因此 intellegere 意为在事物之间辨出意义，也就是理解。

items.en: Intellectualis was a later adjective used for the thinking part of the mind.
items.cn: intellectualis 是后期形容词，用于心灵中思考的那部分。

items.en: English adopted intellectual in the Middle Ages for what belongs to understanding.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪借入 intellectual，指属于理解力的东西。

items.en: The noun intellectual, a person of ideas, dates from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 作名词表示「知识分子」的用法始于十九世纪。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the legere root; the near-meaning group holds other words about minds and thinking.
note.cn: 形近组共享 legere 词根；近义组收其他与头脑、思考有关的词。

entries.definition: The ability to learn, or secret information.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「智力」，也指情报。

entries.definition: Clear enough to be understood.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明白易懂的」。

entries.definition: Good at learning and reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「聪明的」。

entries.definition: Connected with schools and formal study.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学术的」，与学校、正规研究有关。

entries.definition: Careful and thorough in study, like a scholar.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「治学严谨的」。

entries.definition: Appealing to thought more than feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「诉诸思考的」，偏书卷气。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the legere root of reading and the real phrases around this adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用「读」这一词根 legere，并挂上这个形容词的真实搭配。

normal.en: intellect plus -ual: the quality of understanding.
normal.cn: intellect 加 -ual：理解力的性质。

normal.en: Do not steal intellectual property; it belongs to its maker.
normal.cn: 不要盗取知识产权，它属于创造者。

normal.en: An intellectual lives on books, argument, and little sleep.
normal.cn: 知识分子靠书、辩论和很少的睡眠过活。

normal.en: The same root gives intelligence and intelligible.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 intelligence 与 intelligible。

normal.en: Intellectual work tires the mind, not the hands.
normal.cn: 脑力劳动累的是头脑，不是双手。

abstract.en: An intellectual is someone who cannot stop asking why.
abstract.cn: 知识分子是那种停不下问「为什么」的人。

abstract.en: Intellectual life is a conversation carried across centuries.
abstract.cn: 智识生活是一场跨越几个世纪的对话。

abstract.en: Thinking well is the quietest form of courage.
abstract.cn: 好好思考是最安静的一种勇气。

examples.en: He took an intellectual interest in how languages change.
examples.cn: 他对语言如何演变抱有学术上的兴趣。

examples.en: The magazine was written for a general intellectual audience.
examples.cn: 这本杂志是写给一般有学识的读者看的。

examples.en: She became a respected intellectual after publishing two books on law.
examples.cn: 发表两本法学著作后，她成了一位受人尊敬的知识分子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特莱克」——在因特网上猛查资料，成为知识分子

root: 拉丁语 legere「挑选、读」→ inter-「在……之间」+ legere → intellegere「辨出、理解」→ intellectualis「理解力的」→ 英语 intellectual。同族词：intellect、intelligence、intelligible。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: of the mind, fond of ideas, and as a noun, a person of ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：属于头脑的、喜爱思想的，以及作名词指「知识分子」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp-lit desk piled with books while the street stays outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下的书桌堆满书，街道被关在外面。

branches.en: THE CHESSBOARD: the thinking part of a game is on show.
branches.cn: 棋盘这条线：展现的是游戏里思考的那部分。

branches.en: THE LONG TALK: ideas are enjoyed for their own sake.
branches.cn: 长谈这条线：为思想本身而享受思想。

branches.en: THE NEWSPAPER: named persons are asked to speak about ideas.
branches.cn: 报纸这条线：具名的人被请来谈思想。

definition_en: an illegal act or crime; also the act of upsetting someone, a breaking of the rules in sport, and the attacking side in a game
core_image: 一句话像石子打在别人身上，留下看不见的伤痕
scene: 饭桌上有人顺口拿别人的口音打趣，笑声刚起，桌边几个人的脸就沉了下来。 His harmless joke gave offence to half the people at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 offence 是「冒犯、得罪」（第 2 个义项：使别人感到被冒犯）；句意是他那句自以为无伤大雅的玩笑，让半桌人都觉得受了冒犯。画面里有饭桌、碗筷和突然冷下来的气氛。

pos.zh: 罪行；违法行为；冒犯；犯规；进攻

derivatives.zh: 由同族动词 offend 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「犯罪者；违法者」
由同一拉丁词干加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「冒犯的；进攻的」
由 offensive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「冒犯性；令人反感的程度」

senses.title: An illegal act; a crime
senses.definition: an act that is forbidden by law and can be punished by the state
senses.definitionCN: 法律禁止、可由国家加以惩罚的行为
senses.example: Driving without insurance is a serious offence.
senses.exampleCN: 无保险驾驶是一项严重违法行为。
senses.why: Latin offensa named a striking against something, and English narrowed that image to a wrong the law can punish.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 offensa 本指「撞上、触犯」，英语把这幅画面收窄为法律可以惩罚的过错。

senses.title: The act of upsetting someone
senses.definition: the feeling of being insulted, or the act of saying something that hurts someone
senses.definitionCN: 被人侮辱的感受，或说出使人受伤的话这一行为
senses.example: She took offence at his remark about her accent.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿她的口音开玩笑，她为此生了气。
senses.why: If a word can name a blow, it can also name the sting left by a careless remark, so the same noun covers social injury.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指一次打击，也就能指一句无心之言留下的刺痛，所以同一个名词也覆盖人情上的伤害。

senses.title: A breaking of the rules in sport
senses.definition: an action that breaks the rules of a game and is punished by the referee
senses.definitionCN: 违反比赛规则、由裁判加以处罚的动作
senses.example: The referee stopped play for a handball offence.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因手球犯规中止了比赛。
senses.why: A game is a small legal system, so the legal sense of a punishable wrong transfers easily to the pitch.
senses.whyCN: 球赛是一套小型的规则体系，法律上「可受罚的过错」这层意思很自然就挪到了球场上。

senses.title: The attacking side or attacking play
senses.definition: the part of a team or of a game that attacks, as opposed to defence
senses.definitionCN: 一支球队或一场比赛中负责进攻的一方，与防守相对
senses.example: Their offence moved the ball quickly up the left side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的进攻沿着左路快速推进。
senses.why: The word already carries the image of moving against something, so a team pushing forward is called the offence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就带着「朝着某物撞过去」的画面，所以向前推进的一方被称作进攻。

intro.en: Offence is the noun of a Latin verb for striking against, and it reached English through French with both a legal and a personal sense.
intro.cn: offence 是拉丁语中「撞上去」这一动词的名词形式，经法语进入英语，同时带来法律与人情两层含义。

items.en: The verb offendere was built from ob-, meaning against, and fendere, meaning to strike, so it pictured a blow aimed at something.
items.cn: 动词 offendere 由表示「对着、朝向」的 ob- 与表示「打击」的 fendere 构成，画面是朝着某物打过去的一击。

items.en: The noun offensa grew from that verb and meant a striking against, an obstacle, and a wrong that had been committed.
items.cn: 名词 offensa 从这一动词长出，指撞上、障碍，以及已经犯下的过错。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as offense, keeping both the legal sense of a wrong and the sense of being insulted.
items.cn: 古法语把这一名词写作 offense 传入，既保留「过错」的法律义，也保留「被冒犯」的感受义。

items.en: Middle English offence covered crimes, sins and personal slights, and the spelling settled with a c before i.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offence 同时指罪行、罪过和人情上的冒犯，拼写在 i 之前逐渐固定为 c。

items.en: British English keeps offence while American English writes offense, the form closer to Latin offensa.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留 offence，美式英语写作 offense，后者更接近拉丁语 offensa 的拼法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the verb, the American spelling and the word family built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers legal and social words for wrongdoing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的动词、美式拼写与词族；近义组收法律与人情两方面表示过错的词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，义为冒犯别人或犯罪。

entries.definitionCN: offence 的美式拼写，所指的罪行与冒犯完全相同。

entries.definition: An adjective and noun built on the same stem, meaning insulting or used for attack.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词兼名词，义为冒犯的或用于进攻的。

entries.definition: A person who commits an offence or breaks the law.
entries.definitionCN: 犯下罪行或违法的人。

entries.definitionCN: 法律禁止并可由国家惩处的行为。

entries.definition: An act of breaking a rule, a law or an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则、法律或约定的行为。

entries.definition: A rude remark or action that wounds someone's dignity.
entries.definitionCN: 伤害他人尊严的无礼言语或举动。

entries.definition: Behaviour that is illegal or morally unacceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 违法或在道德上不可接受的行为。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for striking, and its family keeps returning to blows that land on people, rules and laws.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「打击」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到落在人、规则与法律上的那一击。

normal.en: Latin fendere means to strike, and ob- means against, so offence is literally a blow aimed at someone.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fendere 意为打击，ob- 意为对着，所以 offence 字面上就是朝人打出的一击。

normal.en: Offence and offend are one family: the verb is the blow, the noun is the blow and the wrong it leaves.
normal.cn: offence 与 offend 同属一族：动词是那一击，名词既是这一击，也是它留下的过错。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the c, American spelling writes offense, which is closer to Latin offensa.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 c，美式写作 offense，更接近拉丁语 offensa。

normal.en: Take offence means to treat another person's words as a blow aimed at you.
normal.cn: take offence 意为「见怪」，就是把他人的话当成朝自己打来的一击。

normal.en: Criminal offence stretches the same word from a rude remark all the way to a punishable crime.
normal.cn: criminal offence 把同一个词从一句失礼的话一直拉到可受惩罚的罪行。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence thrown like a stone across a dinner table: the bruise is invisible, but offence is its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话像石头一样越过饭桌扔过来：伤痕看不见，而 offence 就是这道伤的名字。

abstract.en: One step over the white line on a pitch is an offence, and so is one step over the line of politeness.
abstract.cn: 球场上越过白线一步是犯规，越过礼貌的界线一步也是冒犯。

abstract.en: The same noun covers a rude word and a crime, which shows that harm is only a matter of degree.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词既指一句无礼的话，也指一桩罪行，说明伤害只是程度之差。

examples.en: Driving without insurance is a serious offence.
examples.cn: 无保险驾驶是一项严重违法行为。

examples.en: She took offence at his remark about her accent.
examples.cn: 他拿她的口音开玩笑，她为此生了气。

examples.en: Their offence was too slow to break the defence.
examples.cn: 他们的进攻太慢，打不穿对方的防线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，犯事」——哦，犯事了，就是 offence：失礼也好，犯罪也好，都是犯了事。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a blow that lands where it should not; from there the word divides into crime, personal insult, a sporting foul and attacking play.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落在不该落之处的一击」；由此分出罪行、人情冒犯、体育犯规与进攻一方。

definition_zh: 观众，听众；受众；正式会见
definition_en: the group of people who watch or listen to a performance, the people a work is aimed at, or a formal meeting with an important person
core_image: 剧场里暗下来，一束光打在台上，台下是一片安静的脸
scene: 演出开始前，主持人请全场把手机调成静音。 The audience fell silent as the curtain rose.

senses.title: People watching a show
senses.definition: the group of people who gather to watch or listen to a performance
senses.definitionCN: 聚集起来观看或聆听表演的一群人
senses.example: The audience fell silent as the curtain rose.
senses.exampleCN: 大幕升起时，全场观众安静下来。
senses.why: The Latin base audire means 'to hear', so the word began as a group of listeners and later took in people who watch as well.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 audire 意为「听」，所以这个词最初指一群听的人，后来也把看的人包括进来。

senses.title: People a work aims at
senses.definition: the particular group of people that a book, programme or product is meant for
senses.definitionCN: 某本书、节目或产品特意面向的那群人
senses.example: The magazine knows its audience well.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志很了解自己的读者群。
senses.why: Here nobody is physically present: the audience is imagined by the maker, a target group rather than a crowd in seats.
senses.whyCN: 这里的受众并不在场：它由创作者想象出来，是目标群体，而不是坐在座位上的那群人。

senses.title: Formal meeting
senses.definition: a formal meeting with a very important person
senses.definitionCN: 与极重要人物的正式会面
senses.example: The ambassador was granted an audience with the king.
senses.exampleCN: 大使获准觐见国王。
senses.why: The oldest court sense survives in this phrase: being admitted to be heard by a ruler, which is why the preposition is with.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷里的古老用法在这个短语里保留下来：获准让君主听你说话，所以介词用 with。

items.en: English extended it to any group that listens.

senses.title: The book that holds the entries
senses.definition: an official book or list in which names, events, or amounts are written down and kept
senses.definitionCN: 正式记录姓名、事件或金额并加以保存的册子或名单
senses.example: The parish register records every birth and marriage since 1700.
senses.exampleCN: 这个教区登记簿记录了 1700 年以来每一次出生与婚姻。
senses.why: The Latin verb regerere meant 'carry back': events were carried back into a book so that they would not be lost. The book is that carried-back record.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 regerere 意为“带回来”：发生的事情被带回一本册子里，以免丢失。这本册子就是那份被带回的记录。

senses.title: The machine that rings up a sale
senses.definition: a machine that records the amount of money taken in a sale and keeps a running total
senses.definitionCN: 记录每笔交易金额并累计总额的机器
senses.example: She opened the cash register and counted the morning's takings.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开收银机，清点了上午的收入。
senses.why: Once entries were kept by a machine rather than a clerk, the name of the book moved to the box: the register registers each sale as it happens.
senses.whyCN: 当条目由机器而不是店员来记录，这本册子的名字就转移到了那只箱子上：收银机在每笔交易发生时把它记下来。

senses.title: The range of a voice or instrument
senses.definition: the range of pitches that a voice or instrument can produce, or a part of that range with a distinct quality
senses.definitionCN: 人声或乐器能发出的音高范围，或其中音质独特的一段
senses.example: The soprano's upper register was clear and effortless.
senses.exampleCN: 那位女高音的高音区清亮而毫不费力。
senses.why: A register was first a list, then the compass of a voice — the full list of notes it can reach. The musical sense, recorded in 1811, treats pitch as entries on a scale.
senses.whyCN: register 先是一份名单，再是一个声音的“音域”——它能达到的全部音符的名单。音乐义记录于 1811 年，把音高当作同一把尺子上的条目。

senses.title: The level of language a situation calls for
senses.definition: in linguistics, a style or level of language used in a particular social situation
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指在特定社会场合所使用的语言风格或层次
senses.example: The report was written in a formal academic register.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告用的是正式的学术语体。
senses.why: The musical idea of a range or level was carried into language: a speaker moves between formal and casual registers much as a voice moves between high and low.
senses.whyCN: 音乐里“音域、层次”的观念被带进了语言：说话人在正式与随意之间切换语体，正如人声在高音与低音之间移动。

senses.title: A slot inside a processor
senses.titleCN: 处理器里的一个存储槽
senses.definition: in computing, a small, fast storage location inside a processor that holds one piece of data during an operation
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指处理器内部容量很小、速度很快的存储位置，在一次运算中存放一项数据
senses.example: The program loads both numbers into registers before adding them.
senses.exampleCN: 程序先把两个数装进寄存器，然后再相加。
senses.why: A processor register is a numbered slot where a value is entered and kept, the smallest version of the ledger's ruled line.
senses.whyCN: 处理器寄存器是一个编号的格子，一个数值被“写进去”并保存在那里，它是账簿横线的最小版本。

senses.title: Write it into the record
senses.definition: to write a name, fact, or amount into an official list or system
senses.definitionCN: 把姓名、事实或金额写进正式的名单或系统
senses.example: The clerk registered the deed at the county office.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在县办事处登记了这份契约。
senses.why: This is the verb built directly on the noun: to register is to put an entry into the register.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接由名词构成的动词：to register 就是把一个条目放进登记册。

senses.title: Put your own name down
senses.definition: to add your own name to a list in order to take part in something
senses.definitionCN: 为参加某项活动而把自己的名字加入名单
senses.example: You must register to vote before the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须在本月底之前登记才能投票。
senses.why: The verb turned reflexive in ordinary use: the person becomes both the writer and the entry. This sense is recorded from 1848.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在日常使用中转向了自身：人既是书写者，也是被写下的那一条。这个义项记录于 1848 年。

senses.title: Show a reading on a dial
senses.definition: of an instrument, to show or record a measured value
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器显示或记录某个测得的数值
senses.example: The thermometer registered thirty degrees at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时温度计显示三十度。
senses.why: An instrument registering is the machine doing the clerk's work: it enters the measurement into its own record and displays it.
senses.whyCN: 仪器 register，就是机器在做店员的活：它把测量结果写进自己的记录，并显示出来。

senses.title: Let an expression show
senses.definition: of a feeling, to appear on a face or in a voice before it is put into words
senses.definitionCN: 指某种情绪在说出口之前先显现在脸上或声音里
senses.example: Surprise registered on her face before she spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 她还没开口，惊讶就先显在了脸上。
senses.why: The 1901 sense treats the face as an instrument: the feeling reaches the surface and the dial moves.
senses.whyCN: 1901 年的这个义项把脸当作一台仪器：情绪抵达表面，表盘便动了。

intro.en: Register comes from Medieval Latin registrum, a much altered form of regestum, from Latin regerere 'carry back'. The second -r- was added by analogy, and some later senses were coloured by the unrelated regere 'rule'. Dates follow standard etymological references.
intro.cn: register 来自中世纪拉丁语 registrum，它是 regestum 经过大幅变形的形式，源头是拉丁语 regerere“带回”。第二个 -r- 是类比加上的，后来某些义项又受到无关的 regere“统治”影响。年代依据通行词源资料。

items.en: The noun registre is first recorded meaning 'public record book, private account book, an official written account regularly kept'.
items.cn: 名词 registre 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“公共记录簿、私人账簿、定期保存的正式书面记录”。

items.en: From Old French registre (13c.) and directly from Medieval Latin registrum, regestrum, properly regestum, from Late Latin regesta 'list, matters recorded'. The unetymological second -r- came by influence of Latin nouns in -istrum.
items.cn: 来自古法语 registre（13 世纪），并直接来自中世纪拉丁语 registrum、regestrum，本作 regestum，出自晚期拉丁语 regesta“清单、被记录的事项”。非词源的第二个 -r- 是受拉丁语 -istrum 类名词影响而加上的。

items.en: Regesta is the neuter plural of regestus, past participle of regerere 'to record; retort', literally 'to carry back, bring back', from re- 'back' + gerere 'carry, bear'. The record is what has been carried back.
items.cn: regesta 是 regestus 的中性复数，后者是 regerere 的过去分词，意为“记录；反驳”，字面是“带回、携回”，由 re-“回”加 gerere“携带、承载”构成。记录就是被带回来的东西。

items.en: Some later senses seem to have been influenced by association with unrelated Latin regere 'to rule, to guide, to keep straight'. Regere is not the source of register; the two families only resemble each other.
items.cn: 后来某些义项似乎受到无关的拉丁语 regere“统治、引导、使笔直”的联想影响。regere 并不是 register 的来源；两个词族只是形似。

items.en: The printing sense 'exact alignment of presswork' is from the 1680s. The musical sense 'compass or range of a voice or instrument' is from 1811, hence 'a series of tones of the same quality'. The sense 'device by which data is automatically recorded' is by 1830, from the verb.
items.cn: 印刷义“印件的精确对齐”始于 17 世纪 80 年代。音乐义“人声或乐器的音域”始于 1811 年，由此引申为“同一音质的一组音”。义项“自动记录数据的装置”到 1830 年已出现，来自动词。

items.en: The verb registren 'to record, enter in a listing' is late 14c.; 'enroll someone' is c.1400; instruments 'show a reading' 1797; 'enter one's own name' 1848; persons and feelings 'make an impression' by 1901. Registered nurse is attested from 1879.
items.cn: 动词 registren“记录、列入清单”为 14 世纪晚期；c.1400 起有“使某人登记入册”；仪器“显示读数”始于 1797 年；“写下自己的名字”始于 1848 年；人或情绪“留下印象”到 1901 年已出现。registered nurse（注册护士）见于 1879 年。

note.en: The first group separates register from its derived nouns, each of which names a different part of the act: the process, the office, the official, the person enrolled. The second group compares the verbs of putting something on a list.
note.cn: 第一组把 register 与它的派生名词分开，每个派生词命名这个行为的不同部分：过程、机构、官员、被登记的人。第二组比较几个“把某物列入名单”的动词。

entries.definition: the act or process of registering. It names the procedure, while register is the book or the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 登记或注册的行为与过程。它命名程序，而 register 是册子或动作本身。

entries.definition: an office where records are kept, or a formal list or database. It is the place or the collection, not the single book on the counter.
entries.definitionCN: 保存记录的机构，或正式的名单、数据库。它是场所或集合，而不是柜台上那一本册子。

entries.definition: the official who keeps a register, especially at a university or hospital. It is the person, not the record.
entries.definitionCN: 保管登记册的官员，尤指大学或医院中的注册主任。它是人，而不是记录。

entries.definition: a person who registers, especially for a course, exam, or event. It is the person on the list, not the person keeping it.
entries.definitionCN: 进行登记的人，尤指报名课程、考试或活动者。它是名单上的人，而不是保管名单的人。

entries.definition: to store information so that it can be found later. It is broader than register: you can record a sound or a fact without entering it in an official list.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息存下来以便日后查找。它比 register 宽：你可以记录一段声音或一个事实，而不必把它写进正式名单。

entries.definition: to join a school, course, or organization by having your name entered on its list. It focuses on becoming a member, while register focuses on the act of writing the name down.
entries.definitionCN: 通过把名字列入名单而加入学校、课程或组织。它强调成为成员，而 register 强调写下名字这个动作。

entries.definition: to put your name down for something, usually in everyday speech. It is the informal phrasal equivalent of register for a course or event.
entries.definitionCN: 报名参加某事，通常用于日常口语。它是 register 用于课程或活动时的非正式短语对应语。

entries.definition: to write down events in a regular record as they happen, especially for technical or official purposes. A log is continuous; a register is often a formal list of names or transactions.
entries.definitionCN: 随着事件发生而定期写入记录，尤用于技术或正式目的。日志是连续的；登记册通常是姓名或交易的正式名单。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'back' + gerere 'carry', the Medieval Latin registrum, and the English family registration, registry, registrar and registrant.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-“回”加 gerere“携带”、中世纪拉丁语 registrum，以及英语词族 registration、registry、registrar、registrant。

normal.en: regerere means 'carry back': an event is carried back into a book so that it can be found again.
normal.cn: regerere 意为“带回”：一件事被带回册子里，以便日后还能找到。

normal.en: The second -r- in registrum is unetymological, added by analogy with nouns ending in -istrum. It is not part of the root.
normal.cn: registrum 里的第二个 -r- 不是词源原有的，而是类比 -istrum 结尾的名词加上去的。它不属于词根。

normal.en: regere 'rule' is a different verb. It coloured some later senses but did not father the word.
normal.cn: regere“统治”是另一个动词。它影响了后来某些义项，却不是这个词的来源。

normal.en: The verb has two everyday branches: write something in (register a deed), and put your own name down (register to vote).
normal.cn: 动词有两个日常分支：把某物写进去（登记契约），以及写下自己的名字（登记投票）。

normal.en: An instrument registers a reading, and a face registers a feeling: both are dials that move when something arrives.
normal.cn: 仪器 register 一个读数，脸 register 一种情绪：两者都是“有东西到达时表盘就动”的仪器。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger open on a counter. Every arrival gets one line, and the line stays after the person has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊在柜台上的账簿。每来一个人就添一行，人走了，这一行还留着。

abstract.en: From that book the word spreads in three directions: the machine that writes the lines, the range of notes written on a musical scale, and the slot where a processor keeps one value.
abstract.cn: 从这个册子出发，这个词向三个方向扩散：替人写行的机器、写在音阶上的音域，以及处理器保存一个数值的格子。

abstract.en: Register is about entry, not memory: the point is that the name or number has been formally put in, not that someone remembers it.
abstract.cn: register 的关键是“入册”，而不是记忆：重点在于姓名或数字已被正式写进去，而不在于有人记得它。

examples.en: All births and deaths are registered at the town hall.
examples.cn: 所有出生与死亡都在市政厅登记。

examples.en: The university requires new students to register before orientation.
examples.cn: 大学要求新生在迎新之前完成注册。

examples.en: The gauge registered a sudden drop in pressure.
examples.cn: 压力表显示压力突然下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: “日记斯特”——日记斯特把每天来往的人和账都记进一本厚册子 → register 登记；登记册（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 registrum，上溯拉丁语 regerere“带回、记录”（re- 回 + gerere 携带），核心是“把发生的事带回册子里写下来”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of register, all from one object: a ruled book in which each name, sale, note, or value gets its own line, and the act of putting that line there.
sensesIntro.cn: register 的九个义项都围绕同一件东西：一本划了格子的册子，每个姓名、每笔交易、每个音符、每个数值都占一行；以及把这一行写进去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger open on a counter, one line added for each entry.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本摊在柜台上的账簿，每记一项就添一行。

branches.en: THE BOOK: the original sense is the official volume itself, where names and events are kept in ruled lines.
branches.cn: 册子：最原始的义项就是这本正式簿册，姓名与事件被保存在划好的行里。

branches.en: MACHINES AND SLOTS: the cash register writes the line for us, and the processor register is the smallest ruled slot of all.
branches.cn: 机器与存储槽：收银机替我们写这一行，处理器寄存器则是所有格子里最小的一个。

branches.en: RANGE AND LEVEL: a voice's register is its full list of notes; a language register is the level a situation calls for.
branches.cn: 范围与层次：人声的音域是它全部音符的名单；语域则是场合所要求的语言层次。

branches.en: WRITING NAMES IN: the verb records someone else's entry, or turns reflexive and writes one's own name.
branches.cn: 写入姓名：动词既记录别人的条目，也可转向自身、写下自己的名字。

branches.en: SHOWING: instruments and faces register readings and feelings, as if a dial moved when something arrived.
branches.cn: 显示：仪器与脸分别 register 读数和情绪，仿佛有东西到达时表盘就动了。

intro.en: Register is a Latin-derived noun whose visible ending is -ister/-istery in its medieval forms, not a living English suffix. English builds registration, registry, registrar and registrant on the finished word, and the root gerere also reaches English through gesture, suggest and digest.
intro.cn: register 是源自拉丁语的名词，其中世纪形式里看得见的词尾是 -ister／-istery，并非活的英语后缀。英语在成品词上构成 registration、registry、registrar、registrant；词根 gerere 还通过 gesture、suggest、digest 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regerere 'carry back, record' (re- 'back' + gerere 'carry, bear'). Its past participle regestus became regesta 'things recorded', then Medieval Latin registrum. Gerere is a busy verb: it also gives gesture, digest, suggest, congest and register itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regerere“带回、记录”（re-“回”+ gerere“携带、承载”）。其过去分词 regestus 变成 regesta“被记录的事项”，再变成中世纪拉丁语 registrum。gerere 是个繁忙的动词：gesture、digest、suggest、congest 以及 register 本身都出自它。

items.meaning: a book of carried-back records; to enter in it
items.meaningCN: 把记录带回的册子；登记入册（re- 回 + gerere 携带，经 regestus／registrum）
items.example: The hotel keeps a register of all guests.
items.exampleCN: 旅馆保存着所有客人的登记册。

items.meaningCN: 登记；注册（过程）（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Registration closes on the first of September.

items.meaning: an office or list where records are kept
items.meaningCN: 登记处；注册表（-y 表示机构或集合）
items.example: The land registry holds every title deed.
items.exampleCN: 土地登记处保存着每一份地契。

items.meaning: the official who keeps the register
items.meaningCN: 登记员；注册主任（-ar 表示任职者）
items.example: The registrar signed the marriage certificate.
items.exampleCN: 登记员签署了结婚证书。

items.meaningCN: 登记者；注册人（-ant 表示行为者）
items.example: Each registrant receives a badge at the door.
items.exampleCN: 每位登记者在门口领取一张胸牌。

items.meaningCN: 已登记的；注册的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 这是一个注册慈善机构。

items.meaning: to remove from an official register
items.meaningCN: 注销登记；撤销注册（de- 去除 + register）
items.example: The company deregistered for tax purposes.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司为税务目的注销了登记。

items.meaningCN: 手势；姿态（gest- 承载、表演 + -ure）
items.example: He made a small gesture of welcome.
items.exampleCN: 他做了一个小小的欢迎手势。

items.meaning: to bring an idea under someone's notice
items.meaningCN: 建议；暗示（sug- 在下 + gerere 携带，即“带到下面给人看”）
items.example: Her tone suggested that the plan was already agreed.
items.exampleCN: 她的语气暗示这个计划已经谈妥。

items.meaning: to break down and absorb; a summary
items.meaningCN: 消化；摘要（di- 分开 + gerere 携带，即“分开带走”）
items.example: The body digests food slowly at night.
items.exampleCN: 夜间身体消化食物较慢。

latinEntries.structure: neuter plural of regestus, past participle of regerere

definition_zh: 电路；环行路线；巡回
definition_en: a complete path through which electric current flows, a route that returns to its start, or a regular round of visits
core_image: 电流沿着一圈导线跑回起点
scene: 桌上摊着一块电路板，指示灯一闪一闪。 A loose wire broke the circuit.
sceneCN: 这里 circuit 指「电路」（第 1 个义项：电流可以流过的闭合路径）；句意是一根松脱的导线让电路断开了。

senses.title: A closed path for current
senses.definition: a complete path through which electric current can flow
senses.definitionCN: 电流可以流过的完整路径
senses.example: A loose wire broke the circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 一根松脱的导线让电路断开了。
senses.why: Latin circuitus meant a going around, and electricity repeats that closed loop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circuitus 意为绕行，电流重复的正是这种闭合环路。

senses.title: A circular route
senses.definition: a route that goes around and comes back to the start
senses.definitionCN: 绕一圈后回到起点的路线
senses.example: The race covers a five kilometre circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛跑一圈五公里的环道。
senses.why: The going-around sense named any path that returns on itself.
senses.whyCN: 绕行的意思用来指任何自身闭合的路线。

senses.title: A regular round of visits
senses.definition: a regular series of visits to several places in turn
senses.definitionCN: 依次到多个地点的一轮例行访问
senses.example: The judge travels a country circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 这位法官在乡间巡回审案。
senses.why: Officials who rode from town to town completed a ring of visits.
senses.whyCN: 官员从一镇走到另一镇，正好走完一圈行程。

intro.en: Circuit is Latin for a going around, built from around plus to go.
intro.cn: circuit 在拉丁语中意为绕行，由「周围」与「走」两部分构成。

items.en: Circum meant around on every side.
items.cn: circum 意为四周环绕。

items.en: Ire meant to go.
items.cn: ire 意为走。

items.en: Circuitus named the act of going round.
items.cn: circuitus 指绕行这一动作。

items.en: Circuit kept the legal and travelling senses.
items.cn: circuit 保留了法律与巡行的意思。

items.en: English used circuit for a judge's round of towns.
items.cn: 英语用 circuit 指法官巡视各镇的行程。

items.en: Electricity gave the word its most familiar sense.
items.cn: 电学赋予这个词最熟悉的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ring root, while the meaning group names paths and routes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语圆环词根，近义组列出路径与路线。

entries.definition: a round closed shape
entries.definitionCN: 闭合的圆形

entries.definition: shaped like a circle
entries.definitionCN: 形状像圆的

entries.definition: a show performed in a ring
entries.definitionCN: 在圆环场地演出的表演

entries.definition: a path that returns to itself
entries.definitionCN: 回到自身的路径

entries.definition: a way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处的路

entries.definition: a line along which something moves
entries.definitionCN: 某物移动所沿的线

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin parts, the electric loop and the judge's round.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用两个拉丁语部件、电流环路以及法官巡行。

normal.en: Split circuit into circu and it: a ring plus a going, so a going round.
normal.cn: 把 circuit 拆成 circu 与 it：一个圈加一次走，就是绕一圈。

normal.en: A broken circuit stops the current because the ring is no longer closed.
normal.cn: 电路断了电流就停，因为那个环不再闭合。

normal.en: Short circuit skips the long path, and short-circuit as a verb means to bypass.
normal.cn: 短路跳过了长路径，动词 short-circuit 便表示绕过。

normal.en: The racing circuit is a loop of road, and the lecture circuit is a loop of towns.
normal.cn: 赛车环道是一圈路，巡回讲学是一圈城镇。

normal.en: Circuitous keeps the going-around idea in adjective form.
normal.cn: circuitous 以形容词形式保留绕行的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wire returning to the battery it left.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细导线回到它出发的那块电池。

abstract.en: Picture a car passing the same grandstand again.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车再次经过同一座看台。

abstract.en: Picture a judge's carriage stopping in one more market square.
abstract.cn: 想象法官的马车又在另一个集市广场停下。

examples.en: Water got into the circuit and stopped the machine.
examples.cn: 水进了电路，机器停了下来。

examples.en: They drove one full circuit of the park.
examples.cn: 他们绕公园整整开了一圈。

examples.en: The band spent the summer on the festival circuit.
examples.cn: 乐队整个夏天都在音乐节巡回演出。

core.cn: 核心意象：电流沿一圈导线跑回它的源头。

branches.en: The electric loop is the modern everyday sense.
branches.cn: 电流环路是现代最日常的义项。

branches.en: Any route that returns is a circuit of road.
branches.cn: 任何回到原处的路线都是一圈道路。

branches.en: A judge's round of towns repeats the ring on a map.

branches.en: Wire and road share one closed geometry.
branches.cn: 导线与道路共享同一个闭合几何。

branches.en: A racing loop and a lecture loop both end where they began.
branches.cn: 赛车环道与巡回讲学都在起点结束。

senses.title: A thing that is added
senses.definition: a person or thing that is added to an existing group, collection or place and makes it larger or better
senses.definitionCN: 被加入到已有的群体、收藏或地方之中，使其更大或更好的东西或人
senses.example: The new wing is a welcome addition to the library.
senses.exampleCN: 新建的侧楼是这座图书馆很受欢迎的新增部分。
senses.why: Latin additio comes from addere, 'to give to'; the noun first names the act, then the thing that has been given to the whole.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 additio 出自 addere「给到……上」；这个名词先指「给」的动作，再指被给到整体里的那件东西。

senses.title: The act or process of adding
senses.definition: the act of putting something together with something else, so that the whole is increased
senses.definitionCN: 把某物与另一物放到一起，使整体增加的行为或过程
senses.example: The addition of a lift made the old building usable for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 加装电梯之后，这栋老楼人人都能用了。
senses.why: Before there is a new thing, there is the act of putting it in; the same noun covers both the doing and its result.
senses.whyCN: 先有「放进去」这个动作，才有新多出来的东西；同一个名词既指动作，也指结果。

senses.title: The arithmetic operation of combining numbers
senses.definition: the mathematical operation in which two or more numbers are combined to produce a sum
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多的数合成一个总和的数学运算
senses.example: Children usually learn addition before multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们通常先学加法，再学乘法。
senses.why: Arithmetic keeps the most literal image: one amount is given to another, and the result is the heap counted together.
senses.whyCN: 算术保留了最字面的画面：一笔数被给到另一笔上，结果就是把这一堆合起来数。

senses.title: An extension built onto a building
senses.definition: a new part built onto an existing house or other building
senses.definitionCN: 在原有房屋或其他建筑上加盖出来的新部分
senses.example: They built a small addition at the back of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在房子后面加盖了一个小房间。
senses.why: A building grows the same way a pile does: a new piece is given to the old structure and joined to it.
senses.whyCN: 房子长大的方式和堆东西一样：把新的一块给到旧结构上，并与它接起来。

senses.title: A new member of a family or group
senses.definition: a person, especially a baby, who has recently joined a family, or a new member of a team or group
senses.definitionCN: 新近加入家庭的人，尤指婴儿；也指团队或群体里的新成员
senses.example: The baby is the newest addition to their family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个宝宝是他们家最新添的成员。
senses.why: A person can be the thing given to a household just as a book is given to a shelf; the warmth of the phrase comes from that gift.
senses.whyCN: 人可以像一本书被放上书架那样，被「给」到一个家庭里；这个说法里的暖意正来自这份「赠予」。

senses.title: In addition: besides, as another point
senses.definition: in the phrase in addition, used to introduce one more fact, reason or item after what has already been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in addition，在已说过的内容之后再引入一个事实、理由或项目
senses.example: In addition, the museum stays open late on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，博物馆周五延长开放时间。
senses.why: The noun of adding becomes a linking phrase: one more item is given to the list of things already mentioned.
senses.whyCN: 表示「添加」的名词变成了连接短语：在已经提到的一串内容上再给一项。

senses.title: In addition to: as well as
senses.definition: in the phrase in addition to, used before a noun to mean as well as that thing, not instead of it
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in addition to，置于名词前，表示「除该物之外还」，而不是取而代之
senses.example: In addition to the fee, you pay for postage.
senses.exampleCN: 除了手续费，你还要付邮费。
senses.why: The same gesture is made explicit: one item is given on top of another, and both are kept.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作被说得更明白：把一项加在另一项之上，两项都保留。

senses.title: A chemical addition reaction
senses.definition: in chemistry, a reaction in which two molecules combine to form a single new molecule without losing any atoms
senses.definitionCN: 化学中指两个分子结合成一个新分子、不丢失任何原子的反应
senses.example: The addition of hydrogen to the double bond changes it into a single bond.
senses.exampleCN: 氢加成到双键上，双键就变成了单键。
senses.why: The technical sense is the literal one again: two whole units are joined, and nothing is taken away.
senses.whyCN: 这个专业义又回到最字面的意思：两个完整单位合在一起，什么也没有被拿走。

intro.en: Addition is a Latin noun of action built on addere, and it reached English through Old French with the arithmetic sense already attached.
intro.cn: addition 是建立在 addere 之上的拉丁语动作名词，经由古法语进入英语时，算术义已经附着其上。

items.en: Addere was ad-, 'to', plus dare, 'to give': 'to give to, put to, add'. The root behind dare is a reconstructed Indo-European form meaning 'to give'.
items.cn: addere 是 ad-「向」加 dare「给」，意为「给到……上、放上去、增加」。dare 背后的词根是表示「给」的原始印欧语重构形式。

items.en: The noun additio, 'an adding, an addition', was formed with the action-noun suffix -tio; the stem addit- is what English later took over.
items.cn: 名词 additio 意为「添加、增加」，由动作名词后缀 -tio 构成；英语后来接过的正是 addit- 这个词干。

items.en: Old French addicion carried the word toward English, and the spelling with -tion was restored later under Latin influence.
items.cn: 古法语 addicion 把这个词带向英语，后来在拉丁语影响下又恢复了 -tion 的拼写。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, with both the general sense and the arithmetic sense in use.
items.cn: 这个名词自十四世纪起在英语中有记录，一般义与算术义当时都在使用。

items.en: The linking phrases in addition and in addition to spread in the seventeenth century; the chemical sense of an addition reaction belongs to modern chemistry.
items.cn: 连接短语 in addition 与 in addition to 在十七世纪流行；「加成反应」的化学义则属于现代化学。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the add family plus edition, which shares the gift root under a different prefix; the near-meaning group gathers words for something extra.
note.cn: 形近组收 add 这一族词，外加前缀不同但同出「给」这个词根的 edition；近义组收表示额外之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed, meaning to put one thing together with another.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的动词原形，义为「添加、加上、相加」，名词即由它构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning extra, formed from addition with the suffix -al.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、附加的」，由 addition 加后缀 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A substance added in small amounts to food or fuel; formed with the suffix -ive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」，指少量加入食品或燃料中的物质；由同一词干加后缀 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: A particular version of a book or newspaper; it shares the Latin root dare but not the prefix ad-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本、版次」；与本词同出拉丁语 dare「给」，但用的是前缀 ex-，并非 ad-。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or complete a thing, often sold separately.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充物、增刊」，指为改进或补全而外加的东西，常单独出售。

entries.definition: An extra part added to a building or a period added to a deadline.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「扩建部分、延长期」，指加在建筑上的部分或延长的期限。

entries.definition: An additional item that costs more or is not strictly necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「额外的东西、额外的」，口语常用，指多花钱或并非必需的部分。

entries.definition: A small amount by which something increases, especially in pay or figures.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增量、加薪额」，指某物小幅增加的数量，多用于工资或数据，语气正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Latin noun back to addere and then through the common phrases and school arithmetic.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把拉丁名词追回到 addere，再串起常见短语与学校里的算术。

normal.en: Ad- plus dare gives addere, and additio is simply that verb with an action-noun suffix.
normal.cn: ad- 加 dare 得到 addere，additio 只是给这个动词加上动作名词后缀。

normal.en: In addition and in addition to both keep the new item and never replace anything.
normal.cn: in addition 与 in addition to 都保留被加进来的东西，从不取代原有之物。

normal.en: An addition to a house is a room; an addition to a family is a baby.
normal.cn: 房子上的 addition 是一个房间，家庭里的 addition 是一个宝宝。

normal.en: Addition and subtraction are the first two operations children learn.
normal.cn: addition 与 subtraction 是孩子最先学的两种运算。

normal.en: The adjective is additional, the adverb additionally, and the food substance is an additive.
normal.cn: 形容词是 additional，副词是 additionally，食品里的添加物叫 additive。

abstract.en: A shelf does not become a new shelf; it simply holds one more row.
abstract.cn: 书架不会变成另一个书架，它只是多放了一排。

abstract.en: Adding keeps the old and brings the new; nothing is swapped out.
abstract.cn: 添加保留旧的、带来新的，没有哪一样被换掉。

abstract.en: The same word names the hand that adds and the thing that was added.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指添加的那只手，也指被加进来的那样东西。

examples.en: This chair is a useful addition to the small balcony.
examples.cn: 这把椅子给小阳台添了个实用的位置。

examples.en: In addition to the rent, we pay for water and electricity.
examples.cn: 除了房租，我们还要付水电费。

examples.en: She is studying addition and subtraction this term.
examples.cn: 她这学期在学加法和减法。

root: 拉丁语 additio「添加、增加」由 addere「给到……上」加动作名词后缀 -tio 构成，词干 addit- 进入英语后作 addition；addere 则可拆为 ad-「向」+ dare「给」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one gesture of putting something to something that already exists: the thing, the act, the sum, an extension, a new member, the two linking phrases, and a chemical joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是同一个动作——把某物给到已有之物上：那件东西、那个动作、那个和、扩建部分、新成员、两个连接短语，以及化学上的结合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more row of books is set on a shelf that already holds rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：在已经放着几排书的架子上再放一排。

branches.en: THE THING: what has been given to the whole now stands there as a new item.
branches.cn: 物件线：被给到整体里的那样东西，如今作为新添之物立在那里。

branches.en: THE ACT: the gesture of putting it in comes before the result.
branches.cn: 动作线：先有「放进去」这个动作，才有随之而来的结果。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: numbers and molecules are joined whole, with nothing removed.
branches.cn: 运算线：数字与分子都是整块地合在一起，没有东西被拿走。

branches.en: THE GROWING WHOLE: a house gains a room, and a family gains a member.
branches.cn: 生长线：房子多出一间房，家庭多出一位成员。

branches.en: THE PHRASES: in addition and in addition to place one more item on the list already spoken.
branches.cn: 短语线：in addition 与 in addition to 在已经说出的清单上再放一项。

intro.en: Addition is a Latin verb plus an action-noun suffix, and English builds the rest of the family with -al, -ly and -ive.

latinIntro.en: Addere, additio and additamentum are recorded Latin forms, so only the Indo-European root of dare is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: addere、additio 与 additamentum 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，只有 dare 的印欧词根属于重构。

senses.title: To cook in an oven

senses.definitionCN: 用烤箱的干热把食物烤熟
senses.example: She likes to bake bread on Sunday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢在周日早上烤面包。
senses.why: Bake is an old English word that has always meant cooking with dry heat rather than over a flame.
senses.whyCN: bake 是古英语词，一直表示用干热而非明火来烹饪。

senses.title: To become cooked

senses.why: If you can bake a thing, the thing itself can bake, which gave the word an intransitive sense.
