branches.en: bake in the sun
branches.cn: 在太阳下晒硬

branches.en: freshly baked
branches.cn: 刚烤好的

intro.en: The -er and -ery suffixes give baker and bakery.
intro.cn: 后缀 -er 与 -ery 构成 baker 与 bakery。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词是英语本族词。

definition_zh: 委员会；专门小组
definition_en: a group of people chosen to make decisions or do a particular job for a larger organization
core_image: 长桌旁围坐一圈、举手投票的一群人
scene: 几个人围着长桌，为活动方案投票表决。 The committee met on Monday to review the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 committee 指「委员会」（第 1 个义项：受选处理事务的团体）；句意是委员会周一开会审议这个方案。

senses.title: A group chosen to decide
senses.definition: a group of people appointed by a larger body to decide or manage something
senses.definitionCN: 由更大机构委派来决策或管理事务的一群人
senses.example: The committee approved the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会批准了新预算。
senses.why: A task is committed to a group, and the group takes the name of that trust.
senses.whyCN: 任务被托付给一群人，这群人便承接了这份托付的名字。

senses.title: A smaller working group
senses.definition: a small group formed inside an organization for one particular job
senses.definitionCN: 在组织内部为某项具体工作而设的小组
senses.example: A sports committee organized the summer games.
senses.exampleCN: 一个体育小组筹办了夏季运动会。
senses.why: Large bodies split tasks among small groups, and each is still a committee.
senses.whyCN: 大机构把任务分给小组，每个小组仍称作委员会。

intro.en: Committee is a Middle English noun from the verb commit, meaning a person to whom something is committed.
intro.cn: committee 是中古英语名词，出自动词 commit，本指被托付事务的人。

items.en: Committere meant to entrust something to someone.
items.cn: committere 意为把某事托付给某人。

items.en: Old French commettre and its noun forms carried the sense of trust.
items.cn: 古法语 commettre 及其名词形式都带有信任与托付之意。

items.en: A committe was first one person entrusted with a matter.
items.cn: 最初 committe 指受托办理某事的一个人。

items.en: The meaning shifted from one person to a whole body of people.
items.cn: 词义从一个人转移到一整群人的机构。

items.en: Committee now names any appointed decision-making group.
items.cn: 如今 committee 指任何受委派的决策团体。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns that echo the commit stem, while the meaning group names other decision-making bodies.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 commit 词干相呼应的名词，近义组列出其他决策机构。

entries.definition: the act of sending someone to prison or court
entries.definitionCN: 收押；交付审理

entries.definition: a promise or steady dedication
entries.definitionCN: 承诺；投入

entries.definition: a person who travels to work regularly
entries.definitionCN: 通勤者

entries.definition: a group that manages a company or body
entries.definitionCN: 董事会；理事会

entries.definition: a small group chosen to discuss or judge
entries.definitionCN: 专门讨论或评审的小组

entries.definition: an elected group that governs an area
entries.definitionCN: 管理一个地区的议事机构

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a circle of chairs, then move to the trust behind the title and to smaller working groups.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一圈椅子开始，再走到名称背后的托付与更小的工作组。

normal.en: Committee and commitment come from the same verb, one is people, one is promise.
normal.cn: committee 与 commitment 出自同一个动词，一个是人，一个是承诺。

normal.en: The word ends in -ee, but a committee does the work rather than receives it.
normal.cn: 词尾是 -ee，但委员会是做事的，而不是被做的。

normal.en: A committee meeting is where one decision needs many hands.
normal.cn: 委员会会议，就是一个决定需要许多双手的地方。

normal.en: Set up a committee whenever a job is too big for one desk.
normal.cn: 一项工作一张桌子办不完，就成立一个委员会。

normal.en: Two e and two t hide inside committee.
normal.cn: committee 里藏着两个 e 和两个 t。

abstract.en: Picture a long table with eight chairs and one lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，八把椅子，一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture hands rising slowly for a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象表决时一只只手缓缓举起。

abstract.en: Picture a folder passed from one member to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹在成员之间传递。

examples.en: The committee met on Monday to review the plan.
examples.cn: 委员会周一开会审议这个方案。

examples.en: She joined the school safety committee.
examples.cn: 她加入了学校的安全委员会。

examples.en: The committees will report back next month.
examples.cn: 各委员会下个月提交报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 committee 记成 commit（托付）加 tee：被托付一群人办事，这群人就是委员会。

root: 由动词 commit 派生而来，词根为拉丁语 committere（托付），本义是被托付事务的人，后转指受委派的团体。

sensesIntro.en: From one trusted person, to the body that decides, and finally to any small group given a single job.
sensesIntro.cn: 从受信任的一个人，到作出决定的机构，再到承担单项任务的小组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people around a long table, raising hands to decide.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌旁围坐一圈、举手投票的一群人。

branches.en: The decision-making body is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 决策机构是今天的主要义项。

branches.en: A small group inside an organization is the same idea at smaller scale.
branches.cn: 组织内部的小组，是同一想法在更小尺度上的体现。

branches.en: Both a national body and a school group work by meeting.
branches.cn: 全国性机构与校内小组都靠开会运作。

branches.en: Size changes, but the trust placed in the group does not.
branches.cn: 规模会变，但托付给这群人的信任不变。

branches.en: The smallest committee is often the one that gets things done.
branches.cn: 最小的委员会往往才是真正把事办成的那个。

intro.en: Committee is a noun from commit, and it keeps the doubled t in the singular and plural.
intro.cn: committee 是由 commit 派生的名词，单复数都保留双写的 t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mittere, to send, sits under the whole commit family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere（送出）支撑着整个 commit 家族。

items.example: Three committees share the same room.
items.exampleCN: 三个委员会共用同一间房。

items.example: They commit the matter to a small group.
items.exampleCN: 他们把这件事交给一个小组。
成员们以真正的投入服务。

items.example: The committee is a committed group.
items.exampleCN: 这个委员会是一群尽心尽力的人。

items.meaning: the act of sending someone to prison or court
items.example: The committal was delayed by a week.

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.example: The commission sits with the committee.
items.exampleCN: 这个委员会与那个委员会一同开会。

items.meaning: a smaller committee inside a larger one
items.exampleCN: 一个小组委员会起草了规则。

items.meaning: a male member of a committee

definition_zh: 倾斜；倚靠；倾向；瘦的；精瘦的；（肉）瘦的；紧缩的
definition_en: to bend or rest against something, to tend towards a view, or to be thin, without fat or spare resources
core_image: 一个人把肩膀靠向窗框，身子斜成一条线
scene: 雨夜的车站里，旅人把肩膀靠向窗边的墙，望着外面的水汽。 She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「倚靠、倾斜」（第 2 个义项：把身体靠在某物上）；句意为她靠着窗看雨。可辨识画面：车站、窗边的旅人、玻璃上的水汽。

pos.zh: 瘦的；精瘦的；（肉）瘦的；紧缩的

derivatives.zh: 由 lean 加 -ing 构成，义为「倾向；倾斜」
由 lean 加 -ly 构成，义为「精瘦地」
由 lean 加 -ness 构成，义为「瘦；贫乏」
由 lean 与 to 复合，义为「单坡棚屋」

senses.title: To bend away from upright
senses.definition: to slope or bend away from a vertical position
senses.definitionCN: 偏离垂直位置而倾斜
senses.example: The old fence leans to the left.
senses.exampleCN: 那道旧篱笆向左倾斜。
senses.why: Old English hleonian meant to bend or recline, and the body's tilt is the picture the word starts from.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hleonian 意为弯下、躺靠，身体倾斜的样子就是这个词起笔的画面。

senses.title: To rest against something
senses.definition: to put your weight on something while standing or sitting
senses.definitionCN: 站或坐时把重量放在某物上
senses.example: She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠着窗看雨。
senses.why: If a body bends sideways, it must be held up by something, so the tilt becomes support.
senses.whyCN: 身体若向一侧弯，就得有别的东西撑住，倾斜于是变成依靠。

senses.title: To tend towards an opinion
senses.definition: to favour one choice or view more than another
senses.definitionCN: 更支持某一种选择或看法
senses.example: The committee leans towards a later start.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于晚一点开始。
senses.why: Mind leaning to one side mirrors a body leaning on a wall, so the same verb covers opinions.
senses.whyCN: 心思靠在一边，正如身体靠在墙上，同一个动词便也用来指看法。

senses.title: Thin, without much fat
senses.definition: thin in a healthy way, with little fat and firm muscle
senses.definitionCN: 瘦得健康，脂肪少而肌肉结实
senses.example: The runner had a lean, strong build.
senses.exampleCN: 那名跑步者体格精瘦有力。
senses.why: A separate Old English adjective hlǣne meant thin, and English merged it into the same spelling as the verb.
senses.whyCN: 另有一个古英语形容词 hlǣne 意为瘦，英语把它并入了与动词相同的拼写。

senses.title: Meat with little fat
senses.definition: meat that contains little fat
senses.definitionCN: 含脂肪很少的肉
senses.example: She bought lean beef for the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了瘦牛肉煮汤。
senses.why: Thinness applied to meat simply means the fat has been left out, an easy extension of the bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 「瘦」用在肉上只表示去掉了脂肪，是身体义的自然延伸。

senses.title: Short of money or supplies
senses.definition: limited in money or resources, as in lean years
senses.definitionCN: 钱财或资源有限，如艰难的年头
senses.example: The company survived several lean years.
senses.exampleCN: 公司熬过了好几个艰难的年头。
senses.why: A body without fat has nothing to spare, and a budget in the same state is called lean.
senses.whyCN: 身上没脂肪就没有余量，处于同样状态的预算也被称为 lean。

intro.en: Two Old English words, a verb of bending and an adjective of thinness, were pulled into one spelling in English.
intro.cn: 两个古英语词，一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词，在英语里被拉进了同一个拼写。

items.en: Hleonian meant to lean, bend or recline, and it is the source of the verb.
items.cn: hleonian 意为倾、弯、躺靠，是动词的来源。

items.en: A separate adjective hlǣne meant lean or thin, with no fat to spare.
items.cn: 另有一个形容词 hlǣne，意为瘦、没有多余脂肪。

items.en: Middle English lenen kept the verb, and the adjective was pulled into the same spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语 lenen 保留了动词，形容词也被拉进同一拼写。

items.en: The two words met in form, so one spelling now carries both bending and thinness.
items.cn: 两个词在形式上相遇，于是一个拼写同时承载「倾斜」与「瘦」。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective to meat, budgets and hard years.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词义扩展到肉、预算与艰难的年头。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms of this word and words that differ by a letter; the near-meaning group collects words for thinness and for tilting.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的各种形式以及只差一个字母的词；近义组收表示瘦与倾斜的词。

entries.definition: A tendency to prefer one idea or side.
entries.definitionCN: 偏好某种想法或一方的倾向。

entries.definition: A small shelter with a sloping roof against a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 靠墙搭起、屋顶倾斜的小棚。

entries.definition: In a thin, spare way.
entries.definitionCN: 以精瘦、简省的方式。

entries.definition: A legal claim on property until a debt is paid.
entries.definitionCN: 债务清偿前对财产的法定扣押权；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To jump a long way or suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 长距离或突然地跳。

entries.definition: Having little fat or width.
entries.definitionCN: 脂肪或厚度小的。

entries.definition: Thin in an attractive or graceful way.
entries.definitionCN: 纤细而好看的。

entries.definition: Thin, often used of a deliberate or healthy figure.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦的，常指刻意保持或健康的体形。

entries.definition: To slope or lean to one side.
entries.definitionCN: 向一侧倾斜。

normalIntro.en: A verb of bending and an adjective of thinness share one spelling, so every sense sits between a tilted body and a body with no spare fat.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词共用一个拼写，所以每个义项都落在「倾斜的身体」与「没有多余脂肪的身体」之间。

normal.en: Hleonian is the Old English verb for leaning, and it is the ancestor of the body sense.
normal.cn: hleonian 是古英语里表示倚靠的动词，是身体义的祖先。

normal.en: Hlǣne was a different Old English adjective for thin, so the adjective lean and the verb lean started apart.
normal.cn: hlǣne 是另一个古英语形容词，意为瘦，所以形容词 lean 与动词 lean 起初并不相干。

normal.en: Lean on and lean towards keep the picture of weight moved onto something or someone.
normal.cn: lean on 与 lean towards 保留了「把重量移到某物或某人身上」的画面。

normal.en: Lean meat is meat with the fat cut away, not meat that tilts.
normal.cn: lean meat 是去掉脂肪的肉，不是会倾斜的肉。

normal.en: Lean years are years with nothing to spare, the body sense turned into a budget.
normal.cn: lean years 是没有余量的年头，把身体义转成了预算。

abstract.en: One spelling holds two histories, so context decides whether lean is about a body or about a shortage.
abstract.cn: 一个拼写装着两段历史，所以语境决定 lean 说的是身体还是短缺。

abstract.en: Leaning on something is trust made visible: weight is handed over.
abstract.cn: 靠住某物是看得见的信任：重量被交了出去。

abstract.en: Fat is spare capacity, so a lean body and a lean budget both mean there is no margin.
abstract.cn: 脂肪是余量，所以精瘦的身体与紧缩的预算都意味着没有余地。

examples.en: She leaned against the window and watched the rain.
examples.cn: 她靠着窗看雨。

examples.en: The committee leans towards a later start.
examples.cn: 委员会倾向于晚一点开始。

examples.en: She bought lean beef for the soup.
examples.cn: 她买了瘦牛肉煮汤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离嗯」——身体离开竖直，靠向一边，嘴里还「嗯」了一声；记住 lean 是倾斜、倚靠。

root: 动词来自古英语 hleonian（倾靠），形容词来自古英语 hlǣne（瘦），两词在现代英语中拼写合一。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body tilted onto support; the senses then add opinions, a thin body, lean meat and a lean budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一具斜靠在支撑物上的身体；义项由此加上看法、瘦削的身体、瘦肉与紧缩的预算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shoulder pressed to a window frame, the body a straight line at an angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩膀抵着窗框，身体斜成一条直线。

branches.en: an old fence slowly going sideways
branches.cn: 慢慢歪向一边的旧篱笆

branches.en: a traveller's shoulder against a rainy window
branches.cn: 旅人的肩靠在下雨的窗上

branches.en: a committee raising hands for one option
branches.cn: 委员会为某个选项举手

branches.en: a runner with firm muscle and no spare fat
branches.cn: 肌肉结实、没有多余脂肪的跑者

branches.en: an empty account book in a hard year
branches.cn: 艰难年头里空空的账本

intro.en: Two Old English words, a verb of bending and an adjective of thinness, plus English endings, make up this word.
intro.cn: 两个古英语词，一个表示弯的动词与一个表示瘦的形容词，再加上英语词尾，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: Both the verb and the adjective are Old English, and no Latin cognate is recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 动词与形容词都来自古英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a shelter leaning on a wall

definition_zh: 打扰；使不安；弄乱
definition_en: to interrupt someone, to make someone worried, or to move something out of its place
core_image: 门缝里透出灯光，一只手抬到门边又停住
scene: 他抬手要敲门，看见门缝里的灯还亮着。 Please do not disturb the patient after ten.
sceneCN: 这里 disturb 指「打扰」（第 1 个义项：打断别人正在做的事）；句意是十点以后请不要打扰病人。

collocations.phrase: disturb the papers on the desk

senses.title: To break into someone's work
senses.definition: to interrupt someone who is busy or resting
senses.definitionCN: 打断正在做事或休息的人
senses.example: Do not disturb him while he is writing.
senses.exampleCN: 他写东西的时候别去打扰。
senses.why: A closed door is a small promise that the work continues.
senses.whyCN: 一扇关着的门，是工作还在继续的小小承诺。

senses.title: To make someone uneasy
senses.definition: to make someone feel worried or upset
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到忧虑或难受
senses.example: The quiet in the house disturbed her.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里的安静让她不安。
senses.why: A silence can press harder than a loud voice.
senses.whyCN: 沉默有时比大声说话更压人。

senses.title: To move something out of place
senses.definition: to move or change something that should be left alone
senses.definitionCN: 动了本该原样放着的东西
senses.example: Someone had disturbed the papers on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 有人动过桌上的纸。
senses.why: A moved object leaves a shadow of its former place.
senses.whyCN: 被挪动的东西，会留下原位的影子。

intro.en: Disturb comes from Latin disturbare, from dis-, apart, and turbare, to throw into disorder.
intro.cn: disturb 来自拉丁语 disturbare，由 dis-（分开）与 turbare（搅乱）构成。

items.en: Turba meant a crowd or a noisy confusion.
items.cn: turba 指人群或喧闹的混乱。

items.en: Turbare meant to stir that confusion up.
items.cn: turbare 指把这种混乱搅起来。

items.en: Dis- added the sense of scattering what was settled.
items.cn: dis- 加上把安定之物打散的意思。

items.en: Disturbare described driving a calm crowd into disorder.
items.cn: disturbare 描绘把安静的人群搅乱。

items.en: English used it for breaking another person's quiet.
items.cn: 英语借入时指打破别人的安静。

items.en: Today a noise, a worry or a moved chair can disturb.
items.cn: 今天噪声、忧虑或一把挪动的椅子都能打扰人。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the turbare stem, while the meaning group gathers other ways of breaking in.
note.cn: 形近组共享 turbare 这段词干，近义组则是几种闯入别人状态的说法。

entries.definition: a break in the quiet or order
entries.definitionCN: 安静或秩序被打断

entries.definition: worried, or not at ease
entries.definitionCN: 忧虑或不安的

entries.definition: making people uneasy
entries.definitionCN: 让人不安的

entries.definition: to annoy or trouble someone lightly
entries.definitionCN: 轻度地烦扰别人

entries.definition: to cut into what is being said or done
entries.definitionCN: 打断正在说或做的事

entries.definition: to make someone unhappy or worried
entries.definitionCN: 使某人不快或担忧

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand paused at a lit door and end with papers shifted on a desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只手停在亮着灯的门前开始，落到桌上被挪动过的纸。

normal.en: Dis- plus turb: the calm is stirred into a mess.
normal.cn: dis 加 turb，平静被搅成一团乱。

normal.en: A sign on the door says do not disturb.
normal.cn: 门上挂着一块牌子，写着请勿打扰。

normal.en: The noise outside disturbed her sleep again.
normal.cn: 外面的响声又打扰了她的睡眠。

normal.en: What he saw in the yard disturbed him for days.
normal.cn: 他在院子里看到的东西让他不安了好几天。

normal.en: Do not disturb the wet paint on the rail.
normal.cn: 别碰栏杆上还没干的漆。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to knock, then held still.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起要敲，又停住不动。

abstract.en: Picture a calm pond struck once by a stone.
abstract.cn: 想象平静的池塘被一块石头砸了一下。

abstract.en: Picture a neat pile of papers slid out of line.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠整齐的纸被推歪了。

examples.en: Please do not disturb the class during the test.
examples.cn: 考试期间请不要打扰这个班。

examples.en: The letter disturbed her more than she admitted.
examples.cn: 这封信让她不安，只是她不肯承认。

examples.en: Someone had disturbed the soil near the wall.
examples.cn: 有人动过墙边的土。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disturb 记成「把平静搅散」：dis 表示分开，turb 表示搅乱，好好的一团安静被搅散，就是打扰，也会让人心里发慌。

root: 源自拉丁语 disturbare，由 dis-（分开）与 turbare（搅乱）组成，turbare 又来自 turba（人群、喧闹）。本义是把安静的人群搅乱，后来泛指打断别人的安宁，也指搅乱心思与挪动物件。

sensesIntro.en: From a calm crowd stirred into noise to a neat desk left slightly out of line.
sensesIntro.cn: 从安静的人群被搅成喧闹，到整齐的桌面被弄得略微错位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised to knock, stopping because the light is on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手抬起要敲，看见灯还亮着便停住。

branches.en: The first sense is a break in someone's activity.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是打断别人正在做的事。

branches.en: The second sense is a break in someone's calm.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是打破别人心里的平静。

branches.en: The third sense is a break in the order of things.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是打破物件的原有秩序。

branches.en: Both senses reach a person who did not ask for it.
branches.cn: 两个义项都触到一个并未邀请的人。

branches.en: Both senses can be undone by leaving things alone.
branches.cn: 两个义项都能靠不动手来避免。

intro.en: Disturb belongs to the turbare family, where Latin turba, a crowd, gives words for confusion and trouble.
intro.cn: disturb 属于 turbare 一族，拉丁语 turba（人群）生出表示混乱与麻烦的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin turbare, to throw into disorder, gives disturb and turbulent; dis- scatters the settled calm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 turbare（搅乱）给出 disturb 与 turbulent，前缀 dis- 把安定的平静打散。

items.meaning: the state or act of being disturbed

items.example: She looked disturbed by the call.
items.exampleCN: 那通电话让她显得不安。

items.meaning: thick and unclear, as muddy water
items.example: The river ran turbid after rain.

definition_zh: 处理；操作；把手；触摸
definition_en: to deal with a situation, to operate something, the part of an object made to be held, or to touch with the hands
core_image: 一只手握住门把转动
scene: 她处理问题很冷静。 She handled the problem calmly.
sceneCN: 这里 handle 是「处理」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她处理问题很冷静。

senses.title: Deal with
senses.definition: to deal with a situation, problem, or person
senses.definitionCN: 应对情况、问题或人
senses.example: She handled the problem calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 她处理问题很冷静。
senses.why: Dealing with matters is the central modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 处理事务，是核心的现代义项。

senses.title: Operate
senses.definition: to use or control a machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 使用或控制机器或工具
senses.example: He knows how to handle the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 他知道怎样操作这台机器。
senses.why: To handle a thing is to make it work with the hands.
senses.whyCN: 操作一件东西，就是用手让它运转。

senses.title: Grip part
senses.definition: the part of an object made for the hand to hold
senses.definitionCN: 器物上供手握的部分
senses.example: The handle of the cup is broken.
senses.exampleCN: 杯子的把手断了。
senses.why: The noun names the place the hand takes.
senses.whyCN: 名词指手所握的位置。

senses.title: Touch
senses.definition: to touch or hold something with your hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手触摸或拿着某物
senses.example: Wash your hands after handling raw meat.
senses.exampleCN: 接触生肉后要洗手。
senses.why: The oldest sense is feeling something with the hands.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项，是用手去感触。

intro.en: Handle comes from Old English handlian, to feel or touch with the hands, from hand.
intro.cn: handle 来自古英语 handlian（用手触摸），源于 hand。

items.en: Handlian meant to touch or use with the hands.
items.cn: handlian 意为用手触摸或使用。

items.en: Handlen meant to touch or deal with.
items.cn: handlen 意为触摸或处理。

items.en: Handle named the part made for the hand.
items.cn: handle 指为手而设的部分。

items.en: It came to mean managing a situation.
items.cn: 它转而表示应对局面。

items.en: It also meant operating a machine.
items.cn: 它也指操作机器。

note.en: Handle is compared with look-alike words and words for dealing with things.
note.cn: 把 handle 与形近词以及表示应付事物的词作比较。

entries.definition: useful or near
entries.definitionCN: 方便的

entries.definition: one hand's amount
entries.definitionCN: 一把

entries.definition: an obstacle to jump over
entries.definitionCN: 跨栏；障碍

entries.definition: to deal with something successfully
entries.definitionCN: 设法应付

entries.definition: to make a machine work
entries.definitionCN: 操作

entries.definition: to hold tightly
entries.definitionCN: 紧握

normalIntro.en: To handle is to take something in hand, whether a problem, a machine, or a cup.
normalIntro.cn: handle 就是把东西拿在手里，无论是问题、机器还是一只杯子。

normal.en: She handled the problem calmly.
normal.cn: 她处理问题很冷静。

normal.en: He knows how to handle the machine.
normal.cn: 他知道怎样操作这台机器。

normal.en: The handle of the cup is broken.
normal.cn: 杯子的把手断了。

normal.en: Wash your hands after handling raw meat.
normal.cn: 接触生肉后要洗手。

normal.en: Handle the box with care.
normal.cn: 小心轻放这个箱子。

abstract.en: To handle a thing is to accept its weight.
abstract.cn: 拿起一件东西，就是接受它的重量。

abstract.en: A handle is a promise that the hand belongs there.
abstract.cn: 把手是一种承诺：手该放在这里。

abstract.en: The calm hand steadies the whole room.
abstract.cn: 沉稳的手，稳住整间屋子。

examples.en: She handled the problem calmly.
examples.cn: 她处理问题很冷静。

examples.en: He knows how to handle the machine.
examples.cn: 他知道怎样操作这台机器。

examples.en: The handle of the cup is broken.
examples.cn: 杯子的把手断了。

dict_mnemonic.text: handle 是「处理、操作」，也指「触摸」，名词是「把手」；handle a problem 是处理问题，handle with care 是小心轻放，door handle 是门把手。

root: 来自古英语 handlian（用手触摸），源于 hand；用手去碰、去用，引申为操作与处理，又指为手而设的把手。

sensesIntro.en: Handle means to deal with, to operate, a grip part, or to touch with the hands.
sensesIntro.cn: handle 指处理、操作、把手，或用手触摸。

core.en: The hand taking hold of a thing.
core.cn: 手抓住一件东西。

branches.en: A manager calms a difficult meeting.
branches.cn: 管理者稳住一场棘手的会议。

branches.en: A worker turns a control wheel.
branches.cn: 工人转动控制轮。

branches.en: A hand closes on a door grip.
branches.cn: 手握住门把。

branches.en: Fingers touch a rough surface.
branches.cn: 手指触摸粗糙的表面。

branches.en: The grip part and the act of dealing both begin with the hand.
branches.cn: 把手与处理，都从手开始。

intro.en: Handle forms verbs, agent nouns, and compounds of holding.
intro.cn: handle 构成动词、施动者名词，以及表示握持的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word comes from Old English hand.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，源自英语 hand（古英语）。

items.meaning: the bar used to steer a bicycle

definition_zh: 责任；职责；负责
definition_en: a duty to deal with something, or the state of being accountable
core_image: 一个人双手稳稳托着一件必须照看的东西
scene: 照顾年迈的父母是每个子女的责任。 Caring for elderly parents is the responsibility of every child.
sceneCN: 这里 responsibility 是「责任」（第 1 个义项：应当承担并处理的事情）；句意：照顾年迈的父母是每个子女的责任。

senses.title: A duty to deal with something
senses.definition: a duty to take care of something or to do a job
senses.definitionCN: 照看某事物或完成某项工作的义务
senses.example: Feeding the animals is my responsibility.
senses.exampleCN: 喂养动物是我的责任。
senses.why: The noun is formed from responsible, which comes from a verb meaning to answer in return, so a duty is something you must answer for.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 responsible 构成，而 responsible 源于「回以答复」的动词，因此责任就是你必须作出交代的事。

senses.title: Accountability for a result
senses.definition: the state of being the one who must explain or be blamed for something
senses.definitionCN: 必须为某事作出解释或承担过失的状态
senses.example: The manager accepted responsibility for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 经理承担了延误的责任。
senses.why: To answer for an outcome is to be accountable for it.
senses.whyCN: 对结果作出交代，就是对结果负责。

senses.title: A person or thing in one's care
senses.definition: a person or thing that one must look after
senses.definitionCN: 必须由某人照管的人或事物
senses.example: The children are her responsibility while their parents are away.
senses.exampleCN: 父母不在时，孩子们由她照管。
senses.why: A duty can be embodied in the very person or thing you must care for.
senses.whyCN: 责任可以具体化为你必须照管的某个人或某件事。

intro.en: Responsibility is responsible plus -ity, from Latin respondere, to answer in return, so it names the state of having to answer.
intro.cn: responsibility 是 responsible 加 -ity，源自拉丁语 respondere（回以答复），指必须作出交代的状态。

items.en: Respondere means to answer in return.
items.cn: respondere 意为回以答复。

items.en: Responsum means an answer.
items.cn: responsum 意为回答。

items.en: Responsible means answerable for something.
items.cn: 英语 responsible 意为对某事负责。

items.en: The suffix -ity forms responsibility.
items.cn: 词尾 -ity 构成 responsibility。

items.en: Modern English uses responsibility for duties and for accountability.
items.cn: 现代英语用 responsibility 指职责与问责。

note.en: Responsibility is the state noun of responsible, close to duty and accountability words.
note.cn: responsibility 是 responsible 的状态名词，与表示义务和问责的词相邻。

entries.definition: having a duty
entries.definitionCN: 负责的

entries.definition: in a responsible way
entries.definitionCN: 负责地

entries.definition: not taking proper care
entries.definitionCN: 不负责任的

entries.definition: something one must do
entries.definitionCN: 义务；职责

entries.definition: a moral or legal requirement
entries.definitionCN: 义务；责任

entries.definition: the duty to explain one's actions
entries.definitionCN: 问责；应作解释的责任

normalIntro.en: Responsibility is what you must answer for: the duty is a question waiting for your reply.
normalIntro.cn: responsibility 是你必须作出交代的事：责任就是一个等着你回答的问题。

normal.en: Take responsibility means admit that it is your job.
normal.cn: take responsibility 表示承认这是你的责任。

normal.en: A sense of responsibility is the feeling that you must act.
normal.cn: sense of responsibility 是觉得自己必须行动的意识。

normal.en: Social responsibility means caring about others.
normal.cn: social responsibility 指关心他人。

normal.en: The adjective responsible means having the duty.
normal.cn: 形容词 responsible 意为负有责任。

normal.en: Compare duty: duty is a task, responsibility also includes being accountable.
normal.cn: 对比 duty：duty 是任务，responsibility 还包含问责。

abstract.en: Picture two hands holding a fragile bowl steady.
abstract.cn: 想象双手稳稳托住一只易碎的碗。

abstract.en: Imagine a key kept safe because it opens every door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把因能打开所有门而被小心保管的钥匙。

abstract.en: Think of a lighthouse keeper who never leaves the lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一位从不离开灯火的灯塔看守人。

examples.en: She took full responsibility for the mistake.
examples.cn: 她为这个错误承担了全部责任。

examples.en: Teaching children is a serious responsibility.
examples.cn: 教育孩子是一项重大的责任。

examples.en: The job comes with many responsibilities.
examples.cn: 这份工作伴随着许多职责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「response + ibility」——必须「回应」的事，就是责任；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ spondere（承诺）→ respondere（回以答复）→ responsible（负责的）＋ -ity → responsibility，核心义「必须作出交代的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Responsibility first names a duty, then the accountability for a result, and finally the very person or thing one must care for.
sensesIntro.cn: responsibility 先指职责，再指对结果的问责，最后指必须照管的人或事本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a duty held in both hands like a fragile bowl.
core.cn: 核心意象：像端着一只易碎的碗那样托着责任。

branches.en: A duty is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 职责是日常义项。

branches.en: Accountability adds the answering-for sense.
branches.cn: 问责增加了「作出交代」的含义。

branches.en: The cared-for person or thing embodies the duty.
branches.cn: 被照管的人或事体现了责任。

branches.en: A duty that goes wrong brings accountability.
branches.cn: 职责出错时就会带来问责。

branches.en: Looking after a child is both a duty and a trust.
branches.cn: 照看孩子既是职责，也是信任。

intro.en: Responsibility stacks -ity on responsible, which itself comes from a Latin answering verb.
intro.cn: responsibility 在 responsible 上叠加 -ity，而 responsible 源自拉丁语「答复」动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin respondere means to answer in return, built on spondere, to promise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 respondere 意为回以答复，建立在 spondere（承诺）之上。

definition_zh: 康复；找回；经济复苏；恢复
definition_en: the return to health; the getting back of something lost; the return of an economy to growth; the restoring of data or a state
core_image: 清晨病房窗帘拉开，病人自己坐了起来
scene: 护士推开病房的窗帘，阳光照在床边的轮椅和拐杖上。 Doctors expect a full recovery within two weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 recovery 是「康复」（第 1 个义项：恢复健康的过程）；句意为医生预计两周内可完全康复。画面里可留意：拉开的窗帘、床边的轮椅与拐杖。

senses.title: The return to health
senses.definition: the process of becoming healthy again after an illness or an injury
senses.definitionCN: 在生病或受伤之后恢复健康的过程
senses.example: Doctors expect a full recovery within two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 医生预计两周内可完全康复。
senses.why: The noun names the process rather than the moment, so recovery is the road rather than the arrival.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是过程而非瞬间，因此 recovery 是那条路，而不是终点。

senses.title: The getting back of something lost
senses.definition: the act of getting back something that was lost or taken
senses.definitionCN: 把失去或被拿走的东西重新取回的行为
senses.example: The recovery of the stolen painting took months.
senses.exampleCN: 追回那幅被盗的画花了几个月。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the regaining of property, and health is described as property that has been won back.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是重新获得财产，而健康正是被重新赢回的「财产」。

senses.title: The return of an economy to growth
senses.definition: the period in which trade, output, and confidence rise again
senses.definitionCN: 贸易、产出与信心重新上升的时期
senses.example: The city's recovery after the flood was slow.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，这座城市复苏缓慢。
senses.why: A city or a market that climbs back from a low point repeats the pattern of a body getting well.
senses.whyCN: 城市或市场从低点回升，重复的正是身体痊愈的模式。

senses.title: The restoring of data or a state
senses.definition: the process of bringing stored data or a system back to a working state
senses.definitionCN: 让已储存的数据或系统回到可用状态的过程
senses.example: Data recovery saved the entire archive.
senses.exampleCN: 数据恢复保住了整个档案库。
senses.why: A disk that returns to its earlier state is recovering in the same sense as a body, so the word entered computing unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 磁盘回到先前状态，与身体恢复是同一种意义，因此这个词原封不动地进入了计算机领域。

intro.en: Recovery is the noun of recover: the act of getting back, viewed as a process with a beginning and an end.
intro.cn: recovery 是 recover 的名词：把「取回」视为一个有始有终的过程。

items.en: Recuperare meant to regain, especially what had been lost.
items.cn: recuperare 意为重新获得，尤指失去之物。

items.en: Recuperatio named the act of regaining, the direct model for the English noun.
items.cn: recuperatio 指重新获得的行为，是英语名词的直接范本。

items.en: Old French recovrer supplied the verb from which the English noun was formed.
items.cn: 古法语 recovrer 提供了动词，英语名词由此构成。

items.en: Middle English formed recoverie from the verb with the noun ending -ie.
items.cn: 中古英语用动词加名词词尾 -ie 构成 recoverie。

items.en: Modern English uses recovery for health, property, markets, and data.
items.cn: 现代英语用 recovery 指健康、财产、市场与数据。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for healing and retrieval.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表痊愈与找回的词。

entries.definition: The finding of something new.
entries.definitionCN: 发现。

entries.definition: The bringing of something to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 递送；分娩。

entries.definition: A short account of the main points.
entries.definitionCN: 摘要。

entries.definition: The process of becoming well.
entries.definitionCN: 痊愈；治疗。

entries.definition: Rest and recovery of strength.
entries.definitionCN: 休养；康复。

entries.definition: The getting back of something.
entries.definitionCN: 取回；检索。

entries.definition: A recovery after a fall.
entries.definitionCN: 反弹；回升。

normalIntro.en: The word is recover plus y: the process of getting back, whether health, property, trade, or data.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 recover 加 y：把东西取回的过程，无论是健康、财产、贸易还是数据。

normal.en: Recover plus -y: the process of getting back.
normal.cn: recover 加 -y：取回的过程。

normal.en: The road to recovery is the phrase for a long healing.
normal.cn: road to recovery 是形容漫长康复的短语。

normal.en: An economic recovery is a market getting well again.
normal.cn: economic recovery 就是市场重新恢复健康。

normal.en: Data recovery brings a disk back to life.
normal.cn: data recovery 让磁盘重新活过来。

normal.en: The plural is recoveries, changing y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数是 recoveries，y 变 ies。

abstract.en: Recovery is proof that a low point was not the end.
abstract.cn: 恢复证明了低谷并不是终点。

abstract.en: A recovery is slow because it repeats in time what health does at once.
abstract.cn: 恢复之所以缓慢，是因为它把健康瞬间完成的事在时间里重演一遍。

abstract.en: What a person recovers from becomes part of the person who returns.
abstract.cn: 一个人从什么中恢复过来，会成为归来之人身上的一部分。

examples.en: Doctors expect a full recovery within two weeks.
examples.cn: 医生预计两周内可完全康复。

examples.en: The recovery of the stolen painting took months.
examples.cn: 追回那幅被盗的画花了几个月。

examples.en: Data recovery saved the entire archive.
examples.cn: 数据恢复保住了整个档案库。

dict_mnemonic.text: recover（恢复）加 y（名词词尾）：恢复这一过程，就是 recovery——康复、复苏、找回。

root: recover（恢复）+ 后缀 -y（名词词尾）→ recovery；recover 源自拉丁 recuperare；同族有 recoverable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the process of getting back; the senses move from health to lost property, to trade, and to data.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「取回的过程」；义项从健康，到失物，到贸易，再到数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hospital curtain drawn back, the patient sitting up in the morning light.
core.cn: 核心意象：病房窗帘拉开，病人在晨光里自己坐起。

branches.en: a patient sitting up at dawn
branches.cn: 黎明时坐起的病人

branches.en: a stolen painting brought back
branches.cn: 被追回的被盗画作

branches.en: a market climbing after a slump
branches.cn: 萧条后攀升的市场

branches.en: a damaged disk restored
branches.cn: 受损磁盘被恢复

branches.en: a body and an economy both returning
branches.cn: 身体与经济一同回升

intro.en: The noun is the verb of regaining plus a noun ending, and its family covers the process, the possibility, and the result.
intro.cn: 这个名词是「重新获得」动词加名词词尾，其词族涵盖过程、可能性与结果。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recuperare and its noun recuperatio; English added the native noun ending -y.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recuperare 及其名词 recuperatio；英语加上了本族名词词尾 -y。

items.meaning: in the process of getting back

definition_zh: 仅仅；只不过；只是
definition_en: only, and nothing more than what is named
core_image: 一只空盒子，打开后里面只有一张写着「仅此而已」的纸条
scene: 面试官强调，这份工作需要的不是天赋而是耐心。 The job merely requires patience, not special talent.
sceneCN: 这里指限定范围、排除更多要求（第 1 个义项：仅仅，别无其他）；句意为这份工作只需要耐心，并不需要特殊天赋；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Only and nothing more
senses.definition: used to limit a statement to what is named and exclude anything more
senses.definitionCN: 把陈述限定在所说的内容上，排除更多的东西
senses.example: He is merely a clerk in a large office.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是一家大事务所里的职员。
senses.why: The word draws a boundary around the description and denies any larger claim.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在描述周围画下一道边界，否认任何更大的说法。

senses.title: No more than
senses.definition: used to lower the importance of what follows
senses.definitionCN: 用来降低随后内容的重要性
senses.example: The delay was merely a technical glitch.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误不过是一个技术故障。
senses.why: Here the minimizer deflates significance, telling the listener not to treat the thing as serious.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个「缩小词」给重要性放气，告诉听者不必把此事看得严重。

senses.title: Only a matter of
senses.definition: used before a noun to reduce an issue to one simple factor
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，把问题归结为单一简单因素
senses.example: Success here is merely a question of timing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，成功只是时机问题。
senses.why: The pattern collapses a complex situation into one named factor, often for rhetorical effect.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式把复杂情形压缩成单一因素，常带修辞效果。

senses.title: Not merely
senses.definition: in the pattern not merely, used to say something is more than what is named
senses.definitionCN: 在「不只是」的结构中，表示某物超出所说的范围
senses.example: The law is not merely a set of rules but a social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 法律不只是一套规则，而是一种社会制度。
senses.why: Negating the minimizer opens the scale upward; the sentence promises a larger description to come.
senses.whyCN: 否定这个「缩小词」会把尺度向上打开，句子随即承诺一个更大的说法。

senses.title: Merely by doing
senses.definition: used to say that a small action is enough
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个小小的动作就已足够
senses.example: You can sharpen the image merely by changing one setting.
senses.exampleCN: 你只需改动一个设置就能让图像更清晰。
senses.why: The by-phrase presents the minimum sufficient means, with no extra effort implied.
senses.whyCN: 「通过」短语给出最小充分手段，暗示不需要额外努力。

senses.title: Merely because
senses.definition: used to say that a reason is the only one, often to criticize it as insufficient
senses.definitionCN: 表示这是唯一的理由，常含「理由不足」的批评
senses.example: They rejected the plan merely because it came from a newcomer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝这个方案，仅仅因为它是新来的人提出的。
senses.why: The causal phrase usually carries disapproval: a single reason is treated as too thin.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果短语通常带不赞同：单一理由被视为过于单薄。

senses.title: Merely a formality
senses.definition: used of a step that must be done but has no real effect
senses.definitionCN: 指必须完成却没有实际作用的步骤
senses.example: The signature was merely a formality after the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 决定作出后，签字只是走个形式。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks a procedure kept for appearance, not for function.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定短语指为了外观而保留的程序，而非为了功能。

senses.title: Downplaying in speech
senses.definition: used in conversation to soften a request or defend an intention
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中缓和请求或为自己的意图辩护
senses.example: I was merely asking, not accusing you.
senses.exampleCN: 我只是问问，并不是在指责你。
senses.why: In speech the word protects the speaker from a stronger reading of their act.
senses.whyCN: 在口语中，这个词保护说话者，免得自己的举动被读得过重。

intro.en: Merely comes from the Latin adjective for pure or unmixed, through French and English, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; the deeper origin of the Latin adjective is uncertain, and the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「纯粹的、未掺杂的」形容词，经法语与英语，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚；拉丁形容词的更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The Latin adjective merus means pure, unmixed or nothing but.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词意为「纯粹的、未掺杂的」，引申为「不过是」。

items.en: Old French mier carries the sense of pure or entire into French.
items.cn: 古法语形容词把「纯粹、完整」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Middle English mere means pure or simple, and the modern sense of only develops from it.
items.cn: 中古英语形容词意为「纯粹的、简单的」，现代「仅仅」义由此发展。

items.en: The adverb merely grows out of the adjective with the usual suffix, first meaning purely and then only.
items.cn: 副词由形容词加常见后缀构成，先表「纯粹地」，再表「仅仅」。

items.en: The English adverb is recorded from the late medieval period; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语副词见于中世纪末期，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The deeper root of the Latin adjective cannot be confirmed, and no confident Indo-European source can be named; this uncertainty concerns the root, not the clear Latin origin of the word itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词的更早词根难以确证，无法给出有把握的印欧语来源；这属于词根层面的存疑，而词本身的拉丁来源是清楚的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin pure-root; the second group contrasts limits of scope with measures of small size.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「纯粹」词根；第二组对照「限定范围」与「衡量幅度小」。

entries.definition: Nothing more than; also, pure and unmixed in older use.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、不过是；旧义也指纯粹、未掺杂的。

entries.definition: The superlative of mere, meaning the slightest or smallest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词的最高级，意为最微小的。

entries.definition: The quality of being pure or nothing but; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 纯粹或「仅是」的性质；少见。

entries.definition: Showy but cheap and false; it shares the letters mer- but not the pure-root.
entries.definitionCN: 华而不实、虚有其表的；只共享开头字母，并非同一词根。

entries.definition: No one or nothing else besides the one named.
entries.definitionCN: 除所说的人或物之外再无其他。

entries.definition: Simply, with no more than the named thing; also used for emphasis in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅，没有更多；口语中也用于加强语气。

entries.definition: In a plain way, without complication; sometimes close to merely.
entries.definitionCN: 以简单、不加复杂化的方式；有时接近「只不过」。

entries.definition: A phrase that explicitly denies any larger claim.
entries.definitionCN: 明示否认任何更大说法的短语。

entries.definition: Only just, in terms of quantity or degree, not scope.
entries.definitionCN: 就数量或程度而言「刚刚够」，不是限定范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pure-root, the real limiting patterns and the real speech use for softening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「纯粹」词根、真实的限定句式，以及口语中缓和语气的真实用法。

normal.en: The root means pure or unmixed, so merely strips a statement down to one item.
normal.cn: 词根意为「纯粹、未掺杂」，所以这个词把一句话削到只剩一项。

normal.en: Not merely is the door that opens upward: there is always more to say.
normal.cn: 「不只是」是一扇向上的门：后面总有更多话要说。

normal.en: Merely by changing one setting shows how small the sufficient action can be.
normal.cn: 「只需改一个设置」说明充分行动可以多小。

normal.en: Merely because usually sounds like a complaint about a thin reason.
normal.cn: 「仅仅因为」听上去通常是在抱怨理由太薄。

normal.en: In an argument, merely asking is a shield, not a question.
normal.cn: 在争执中，「只是问问」是一面盾牌，而不是一个问题。

abstract.en: Limiting a thing to its name is a way of refusing to let it grow.
abstract.cn: 把事物限定在它的名称上，就是拒绝让它长大。

abstract.en: The word is small but it draws a hard line around a whole claim.
abstract.cn: 这个词很短，却在整段断言周围画出硬线。

abstract.en: Saying merely is often a way to be modest and firm at the same time.
abstract.cn: 说「仅仅」，常常是既谦逊又坚定。

examples.en: The change was merely cosmetic and fooled no one.
examples.cn: 这个改动只是表面功夫，骗不了任何人。

examples.en: She was not merely tired; she was ill.
examples.cn: 她不只是累了，而是病了。

examples.en: The fee is merely a formality to cover paperwork.
examples.cn: 这笔费用只是覆盖文书工作的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「秘而利」——秘密很小，仅此而已

root: 拉丁语形容词「纯粹的、未掺杂的」经古法语与中古英语进入英语，先表「纯粹」，再发展出「仅仅」；副词由该形容词加后缀构成。直接拉丁来源清楚，但其更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate bare limitation, lowered importance, a single-factor reduction, the not-merely expansion, minimum means, a thin reason, an empty formality and polite downplaying.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理纯粹的限定、降低重要性、归结为单一因素、「不只是」的扩展、最小手段、单薄理由、空洞形式，以及礼貌淡化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty box that contains only a slip reading nothing more.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只空盒子，里面只有一张写着「仅此而已」的纸条。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: the statement stops at what is named.
branches.cn: 边界：陈述停在所说的内容上。

branches.en: THE DEFLATION: lowering importance and reducing an issue to one factor.
branches.cn: 放气：降低重要性，把问题压成单一因素。

branches.en: THE OPEN SCALE: not merely promises something larger beyond the name.
branches.cn: 打开的尺度：「不只是」承诺名称之外还有更大内容。

branches.en: THE THIN SUFFICIENCY: the smallest means and the weakest reason.
branches.cn: 单薄的充分性：最小手段与最弱理由。

branches.en: THE EMPTY SHELL: a formality without effect and a polite shield in speech.
branches.cn: 空壳：无实效的形式与口语中的礼貌盾牌。

intro.en: Merely is a Latin pure-adjective, a French layer and an English adverb suffix; the deeper root of the Latin adjective is genuinely uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「纯粹」形容词、法语层与英语副词后缀构成；拉丁形容词的更早词根确实存疑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective for unmixed supplies the whole family, and its deeper origin cannot be traced with confidence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「未掺杂」形容词提供整个词族，其更早来源无法有把握地追溯。

items.example: The adjective describes wine with nothing added.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述没有掺入别物的酒。

items.example: The noun shows how concrete the image of purity first was.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词说明「纯」最初有多具体。

items.example: A related adjective keeps the same physical sense.
items.exampleCN: 一个相关形容词保留同样的具体含义。

items.example: French carries the sense forward before English borrows it.
items.exampleCN: 法语在英语借入前把这一含义传下去。

items.example: English shifts from purity to bare limitation.
items.exampleCN: 英语从「纯粹」转向「仅仅」这一限定义。

items.example: The superlative survives in phrases about the smallest trace.
items.exampleCN: 最高级仍保存在表示「最细微痕迹」的短语里。

items.example: The rare noun names the quality of being nothing more.
items.exampleCN: 这个少见名词命名「别无其他」的性质。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a limiter adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成限定副词。

items.example: The adverb is the form that limits a whole statement.
items.exampleCN: 副词形式用来限定整句陈述。

definition_zh: 音量；体积、容积；量、数额；（书的）卷、册
definition_en: the loudness of sound; the amount of space something fills; a quantity; one book of a set
core_image: 旋钮拧大的一格：同一台机器，装下更多、响过更多
scene: 深夜的书房里，他把收音机的旋钮轻轻拧小。 Please turn down the volume.
sceneCN: 这里 volume 是「音量」（第 1 个义项：声音的大小）；句意为请把音量调低。一格一格拧动的旋钮，就是这个词。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「容量的、按体积计的」，由 volume 加 -ric 构成
形容词，义为「体积大的；著述多的」，由同根加后缀构成
名词，义为「容积计」，较少使用

senses.title: Loudness of sound
senses.definition: how loud or soft a sound is
senses.definitionCN: 声音的大小强弱
senses.example: Please turn down the volume.
senses.exampleCN: 请把音量调低。
senses.why: A rolled scroll holds more; sound fills the room the way a roll fills space.
senses.whyCN: 成卷之物容纳更多；声音充满房间，正如卷轴充满空间。

senses.title: Space filled
senses.definition: the amount of three-dimensional space an object takes up
senses.definitionCN: 物体占据的三维空间大小
senses.example: The tank measures a volume of four cubic meters.
senses.exampleCN: 这个水箱的容积为四立方米。
senses.why: How much space a thing rolls out into is its volume.
senses.whyCN: 一件东西铺开占据多少空间，即是它的体积。

senses.title: Amount or quantity
senses.definition: the total amount or number of something, especially in business
senses.definitionCN: 某物的总量或总数，尤其用于商业
senses.example: Trade volume doubled after the new port opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新港口启用后贸易额翻了一番。
senses.why: Space becomes counting: how much flows through, like water through a channel.
senses.whyCN: 空间之量转为数目之量：流过多少，如水过渠道。

senses.title: A book of a set
senses.titleCN: 卷、册：成套书籍中的一本
senses.definition: one physical book, especially one of a multi-book work
senses.definitionCN: 一本实体书，尤指多卷本著作中的一册
senses.example: Volume three of the encyclopedia came out first.
senses.exampleCN: 这套百科全书的第三卷最先出版。
senses.why: Latin volumen is a rolled papyrus; books began as rolls, so a book keeps the roll's name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 volumen 指莎草纸卷；书起初就是卷轴，成册的书沿用了「卷」的名字。

intro.en: Volume comes from Latin volumen, a roll of writing, from volvere, to roll.
intro.cn: volume 源自拉丁语 volumen（书写纸卷），出自动词 volvere（滚动）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wel- means to turn or roll, behind wheel and volvere alike.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wel- 意为转动或滚动，是 wheel 与 volvere 的共同来源。

items.en: Volvere means to roll; volumen is the thing rolled, a scroll of papyrus.
items.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 意为滚动；volumen 即卷起之物——莎草纸卷。

items.en: Volumen extends to any written work, since works were read in rolls.
items.cn: volumen 引申指任何成文著作，因当时著作以卷轴形式阅读。

items.en: The word becomes volum(e) in French, passing into English with the book sense.
items.cn: 该词在法语中作 volum(e)，带着「书卷」义进入英语。

items.en: English first uses volume for a book, then for bulk or capacity, and later for loudness with sound technology.
items.cn: 英语先指书册，再指体量与容量，随声学技术发展又指响度。

note.en: Look-alikes share the roll-root; near meanings cover amounts, sizes, and loudness.
note.cn: 形近组共享「滚动」词根，近义组涵盖数量、尺寸与响度。

entries.definition: large in bulk; writing much
entries.definitionCN: 体积庞大的；著述丰硕的；volume 的形容词形式

entries.definition: to turn around a center
entries.definitionCN: 旋转；re- 加 volvere，同「滚动」词根

entries.definition: to include or draw in
entries.definitionCN: 涉及、卷入；in- 加 volvere，字面「滚进去」

entries.definition: a pillar or a vertical list in a table
entries.definitionCN: 柱、专栏；与 volume 拼写相近，词根为拉丁 columna（柱），不同源

entries.definition: a curtainlike membrane or covering, technical
entries.definitionCN: 帆状膜、覆盖膜；词根为拉丁 velum（帆），与 volume 不同源

entries.definition: how much a container can hold
entries.definitionCN: 容量；与容积义相邻，capacity 强调可容纳

entries.definition: the quality of being loud
entries.definitionCN: 响度；与音量义相邻的声学词

entries.definition: an amount or number
entries.definitionCN: 数量；与量义相邻，偏可数

entries.definition: large size or mass
entries.definitionCN: 体积、大块；偏大宗感

entries.definition: a large heavy book
entries.definitionCN: 大部头书；与卷册义相邻，偏厚重

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from Latin volvere, to roll.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 volvere（滚动）。

normal.en: volvere means to roll; volumen is a rolled scroll of papyrus.
normal.cn: volvere 意为滚动；volumen 是卷起的莎草纸卷。

normal.en: involve is to roll something in; revolve is to roll again and again.
normal.cn: involve 是滚进去（卷入），revolve 是反复滚（旋转）。

normal.en: a set of books is still called volumes, one roll each.
normal.cn: 成套的书至今叫 volumes，一册即一卷。

normal.en: the volume knob rolls sound bigger or smaller.
normal.cn: 音量旋钮把声音「滚」大或滚小。

normal.en: voluminous describes a dress or a writer that takes much space.
normal.cn: voluminous 形容占空间大的裙摆或多产的作家。

abstract.en: A scroll unrolling across a desk: the space it claims is its volume.
abstract.cn: 桌上徐徐展开的卷轴：它占据的空间就是它的 volume。

abstract.en: A knob turning one notch at a time: the room grows quieter.
abstract.cn: 旋钮一格一格转动：房间渐渐安静。

abstract.en: Shelf after shelf of matching spines: ten volumes, one work.
abstract.cn: 书脊排成一列又一列：十卷书，一部著作。

examples.en: The engine's volume made conversation impossible.
examples.cn: 发动机的音量让人无法交谈。

examples.en: The factory raised its production volume last quarter.
examples.cn: 工厂上个季度提高了产量。

examples.en: Her diary filled five volumes before she turned thirty.
examples.cn: 三十岁前她的日记已写满五册。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我流目」——我放眼量出体积与音量；书一卷卷展开如流水铺目。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 volumen（纸卷）。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（滚动）→ volumen（卷起之物、纸卷）→ 古法语 volum → 英语 volume。印欧词根 *wel-（重构形式）同时衍生 wheel、evolve、revolve 等。

sensesIntro.en: One rolled word grows four ways: the loudness that fills, the space that holds, the amount that flows, and the book that unrolls.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「卷」字四个方向生长：充满房间的响度、容纳的体积、流动的量、展开的书卷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the rolled thing claiming space
core.cn: 核心意象：卷起之物占据的空间

branches.en: The roll measured in three dimensions
branches.cn: 以三维度量的卷：体积

branches.en: The roll counted as it flows through
branches.cn: 流转中被计数的卷：数额

branches.en: The roll that fills a room with sound
branches.cn: 以声响充满房间的卷：音量

branches.en: The roll that became a book
branches.cn: 变成书的卷：册

branches.en: All three quantities answer one question: how much
branches.cn: 三种量回答同一个问题：有多少

intro.en: The roll-root turns through prefixes into some of the most common verbs in English.
intro.cn: 「滚动」词根加前缀，转出英语最常用的一批动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere rolls in every direction its prefixes point.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 随前缀指向各个方向滚动。

items.meaningCN: 轮子，同印欧词根的日耳曼亲属词

definition_zh: 纪律；训练；学科；惩罚
definition_en: training that produces obedience and control, a field of study, or punishment
core_image: 操场上鞋跟并拢的响声，一排人影在晨光里排成直线
scene: 天还没亮，哨声一响，所有人从床上弹起，几十秒后站成四列。 Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 discipline 指「纪律」（第 1 个义项：让人守规矩的约束）；句意是良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。

senses.title: Training that makes people obey
senses.definition: training and rules that produce order and self-control
senses.definitionCN: 带来秩序与自制的训练和规则
senses.example: Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。
senses.why: A line of people moves as one only when each one holds still.
senses.whyCN: 一排人只有各自站住，才能像一个整体那样动。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: a branch of knowledge studied in school or research
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或研究中钻研的一个知识分支
senses.example: She studies two disciplines at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她同时学两门学科。
senses.why: A mind in training is organised like a body in training.
senses.whyCN: 受训的心，和受训的身体一样有条理。

senses.title: To punish and correct
senses.definition: to train someone by punishment or firm control
senses.definitionCN: 用惩罚或严格管束来训练某人
senses.example: The teacher disciplined the class firmly.
senses.exampleCN: 老师严格管教了这个班。
senses.why: The word turns from the rule into the hand that enforces it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从规矩本身，转成执行规矩的那只手。

intro.en: Discipline comes from Latin disciplina, instruction, from discere, to learn, and discipulus, a learner.
intro.cn: discipline 来自拉丁语 disciplina（教导），词根 discere 意为学习，discipulus 指学习者。

items.en: Discere meant to learn, and discipulus meant a learner.
items.cn: discere 指学习，discipulus 指学习者。

items.en: Disciplina named teaching, knowledge and orderly conduct.
items.cn: disciplina 指教导、知识以及有秩序的行为。

items.en: Discipline carried the sense of instruction and correction.
items.cn: 这个词在古法语里兼指教导与纠正。

items.en: English discipline meant training, especially of the mind.
items.cn: 英语里的 discipline 指训练，尤指心智的训练。

items.en: It widened to a field of study and to punishment.
items.cn: 它后来扩展到学科，也指惩罚。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the discip- stem, while the meaning group names order, training and correction.
note.cn: 形近组共用 discip 这一段词干，近义组则区分秩序、训练与纠正。

entries.definition: a person who follows and learns from a teacher
entries.definitionCN: 跟随老师学习的弟子

entries.definition: connected with the punishment of faults
entries.definitionCN: 与惩戒过失有关的

entries.definition: able to control one's own behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 能控制自己行为的

entries.definition: the process of teaching a skill through practice
entries.definitionCN: 通过练习教授技能的过程

entries.definition: a state in which everything is in its right place
entries.definitionCN: 万物各在其位的状态

entries.definition: a penalty given for a wrong act
entries.definitionCN: 对错误行为施加的惩处

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a whistle at dawn to a subject that trains the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从黎明的一声哨响，走到一门训练心智的学问。

normal.en: Discipline and disciple share a root: both are about learning.
normal.cn: discipline 与 disciple 同根，都和学习有关。

normal.en: A line of shoes on a field is discipline you can see.
normal.cn: 操场上排齐的鞋，是看得见的纪律。

normal.en: Self-discipline is a whistle nobody has to blow.
normal.cn: 自律是一声不需要别人吹的哨。

normal.en: A discipline is also a subject, trained like a muscle.
normal.cn: 学科也是一门功夫，要像肌肉一样练。

normal.en: To discipline a child is to teach, not only to punish.
normal.cn: 管教孩子是为了教，不只是为了罚。

abstract.en: Picture four rows of shadows standing perfectly still.
abstract.cn: 想象四排影子一动不动地站着。

abstract.en: Picture a whistle cutting through cold morning air.
abstract.cn: 想象一声哨响划过清冷的晨空。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook filled with the same careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记，全是同样工整的字迹。

examples.en: Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
examples.cn: 良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。

examples.en: She studies two disciplines at once.
examples.cn: 她同时学两门学科。

examples.en: The teacher disciplined the class firmly.
examples.cn: 老师严格管教了这个班。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discipline 记成「地是三坡林」：地在三面坡上，林子里的人也得排好队，讲的就是纪律。

root: 来自拉丁语 disciplina（教导），词根是 discere（学习），同源词 discipulus 指学习者。它先指对心智与行为的训练，后来既指一群人遵守的秩序，也指学校里的一门学问，还引申为用惩罚来纠正。

sensesIntro.en: From a body trained to stand in line, to a mind trained in one field, to the hand that corrects.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被训练得站成一条线的身体，到在一个领域受训的心，再到那只纠正人的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of people standing still at the sound of a whistle.
core.cn: 核心意象：哨声一响，一排排人静静站定。

branches.en: The first sense is the order that training produces.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是训练带来的秩序。

branches.en: The second sense is the field a trained mind works in.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是受训的心所钻研的领域。

branches.en: The third sense is the correction that keeps the order.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是维持秩序的纠正。

branches.en: A trained body and a trained mind follow the same habit.
branches.cn: 受训的身体和心智，遵循同一种习惯。

branches.en: Without correction, the line slowly bends.
branches.cn: 没有纠正，那条线就会慢慢弯掉。

intro.en: Discipline gathers the discip- family, words about learning, order and correction.
intro.cn: discipline 聚起 discip 一族词，围绕学习、秩序与纠正。

latinIntro.en: Latin discere, to learn, gives discipulus, a learner, and disciplina, teaching.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discere（学习）给出 discipulus（学习者）与 disciplina（教导）。

items.exampleCN: 这所学校以纪律严明著称。

items.meaning: a learner who follows a teacher
items.example: He was a disciple of the old master.
items.exampleCN: 他是那位老大师的弟子。

items.example: The company began a disciplinary hearing.

items.meaning: a person who enforces strict rules
items.example: The coach was a firm disciplinarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位教练纪律要求很严。

items.meaning: the act of training or correcting
fields of study or sets of rules

definition_zh: 可接受的；尚可的；合意的；允许的；可以忍受的；合乎语法的
definition_en: good enough to be agreed to, allowed, or tolerated, even though it may not be excellent
core_image: 一只手把东西递出去，对方点点头把它接住：够格，才被收下
scene: 房东把租金写在一张纸上，双方商量了好一阵。 After a long talk, they agreed on a price acceptable to both of them.
sceneCN: 这里 acceptable 指「双方都能接受」（第 2 个义项：能被相关各方同意）；句意为谈了很久之后，他们商定了一个双方都能接受的价格。

pos.zh: 形容词：可接受的；尚可的；合意的；允许的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可接受性；可容许的程度」
由形容词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可以接受地；还算过得去地」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「不能接受的；不可容忍的」
由动词 accept 加后缀 -ance 构成，义为「接受；认可；接纳」

senses.title: Good enough to pass
senses.definition: of a quality or standard, good enough to be approved although not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 指质量或水准虽不优秀，但已达到可以通过的程度
senses.example: The food was plain but acceptable.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜简单，但还过得去。
senses.why: The Latin root means to receive; what can be received is, at the very least, good enough to take in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「接收」；能被收下的东西，最低限度就是达到了可以接受的程度。

senses.title: Agreeable to the people involved
senses.definition: of an offer, price, or plan, able to be agreed to by everyone concerned
senses.definitionCN: 指提议、价格或方案能被相关各方同意
senses.example: They finally found terms acceptable to both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 他们终于找到了双方都能接受的条件。
senses.why: Being received turns into being agreed to: the thing is not merely tolerated, it is taken by both hands.
senses.whyCN: 「被收下」进一步变成「被同意」：这样东西不只是被容忍，而是被双方一起接了过去。

senses.title: Proper in social behaviour
senses.definition: of behaviour, dress, or language, considered proper by most people in a society
senses.definitionCN: 指行为、衣着或语言被社会上多数人视为得体
senses.example: Short skirts were not considered acceptable at the office then.
senses.exampleCN: 那时在办公室里，短裙被认为不合规矩。
senses.why: Society is the receiver here: an act is acceptable when the group is willing to take it in without objection.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「接收者」是社会：一个行为若群体愿意毫无异议地接纳，就是合乎规范的。

senses.title: Permitted by a rule
senses.definition: allowed by a law, rule, or person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 指法律、规定或有权威的人所允许
senses.example: Is it acceptable to park here after six?
senses.exampleCN: 六点以后在这里停车可以吗？
senses.why: The receiver becomes an authority that lets the thing pass; what is let through is acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 接收者变成了放行的权威：被放行通过的东西，就是被允许的。

senses.title: Possible to endure
senses.definition: of pain, noise, or a hard condition, bearable rather than pleasant
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛、噪音或艰难处境尚能承受，谈不上舒服
senses.example: The noise from the road was acceptable once the windows were closed.
senses.exampleCN: 关上窗以后，路上的噪音还算能忍受。
senses.why: Enduring is a slow way of receiving: the body keeps taking the discomfort without pushing it away.
senses.whyCN: 忍受是一种缓慢的接收：身体持续接纳这份不适，而没有把它推开。

senses.title: Welcome and pleasing
senses.definition: of a gift, offering, or act, pleasing and gladly received, in a rather formal use
senses.definitionCN: 指礼物、供奉或行为令人满意、被欣然接受，属较正式的用法
senses.example: The villagers brought offerings acceptable to the river god.
senses.exampleCN: 村民献上了河神愿意接受的供品。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: acceptable simply meant that a person or a god was glad to receive the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：acceptable 原本只表示某人或神明乐于把它收下。

senses.title: Well formed in grammar
senses.definition: in linguistics, of a sentence or phrase, following the rules of the language so that native speakers accept it
senses.definitionCN: 语言学用语，指句子或短语符合该语言的规则，母语者认为可以成立
senses.example: The sentence is odd in meaning but grammatically acceptable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子意思古怪，但语法上是可接受的。
senses.why: Grammar is a set of rules that decide what a language community will receive as a valid sentence.
senses.whyCN: 语法是一套规则，用来决定语言共同体愿意接收什么为合法句子。

senses.title: Valid for an official purpose
senses.definition: of a document, card, or method of payment, recognized as valid by the person or office receiving it
senses.definitionCN: 指证件、卡或支付方式被接收一方认可为有效
senses.example: A passport is the only acceptable proof of identity here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，护照是唯一被认可的身份证明。
senses.why: The receiver checks the thing before taking it; only what passes that check is acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 接收方先查验再收下；只有通过这道检查的东西才是可用的。

intro.en: Acceptable is a Latin word built on the verb 'to take', carried into English through Old French.
intro.cn: acceptable 是建立在拉丁语「拿取」动词之上的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp'. The deeper origin of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿取、抓住、握住」；这个更早的词根来源不确定。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus capere formed accipere, 'to receive, take to oneself'.
items.cn: ad-「向、朝」加 capere 构成 accipere，意为「接收、收为己有」。

items.en: The frequentative acceptare meant 'to receive repeatedly, to welcome', adding the idea of a willing reception.
items.cn: 反复动词 acceptare 意为「一再接收、欢迎」，加入了「乐意接纳」的意思。

items.en: Acceptabilis meant 'that may be received or approved', from which the English word descends through Old French.
items.cn: acceptabilis 意为「可以被接收或认可的」，英语词由此经古法语传承而来。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fourteenth century with the senses of pleasing and of worth receiving.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个形容词，当时兼有「令人满意」与「值得接受」两义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same taking root; the near-meaning group lists words for what can pass a standard.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「拿取」词根构成的词；近义组列出表示「能达标、能过关」的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to take something that is offered.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受、收下」别人递来的东西。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of receiving or approving something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受、认可、接纳」，指接收或批准的行为。

entries.definition: The noun for how far something can be accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可接受性」，指某事物能被接受的程度。

entries.definition: The negative adjective meaning too bad to be allowed or tolerated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不能接受的、不可容忍的」，是本词加否定前缀构成的反义形式。

entries.definition: Good enough to meet a requirement, with a slightly more formal and official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人满意的、符合要求的」，语气比 acceptable 更正式、更像评语。

entries.definition: Bearable but not pleasant, used mainly of pain, heat, or noise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可以忍受的」，多用于疼痛、酷热或噪音，不含满意之意。

entries.definition: Enough in amount or good enough in quality, with an emphasis on sufficiency.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「足够的、尚可的」，重点在数量或程度够用，而非被认可。

entries.definition: Allowed by rules or law, used when the question is permission rather than quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可允许的」，用于讨论规则是否准许，而非质量好坏。

entries.definition: Just good enough to pass, often with a hint of faint praise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「勉强过得去的」，常带一点「只好如此」的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of taking and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「拿取」动词，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: accipere is to receive: acceptable means able to be received.
normal.cn: accipere 是「接收」：acceptable 就是「能被接收的」。

normal.en: The same root gives accept, acceptance and acceptability.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 accept、acceptance 与 acceptability。

normal.en: A price acceptable to both sides is a price nobody rejects.
normal.cn: 「a price acceptable to both sides」就是没有人拒绝的价格。

normal.en: Socially acceptable describes what a group will take without complaint.
normal.cn: socially acceptable 描述的是一个群体愿意无异议接纳的东西。

normal.en: The negative form is simply un- plus acceptable.
normal.cn: 否定形式就是 un- 加上 acceptable。

abstract.en: Picture a doorman who nods: whatever he lets through is acceptable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个点头的守门人：他放过去的东西，就是可接受的。

abstract.en: Acceptance is a scale with a low bar, not a high prize.
abstract.cn: 「被接受」是一道低门槛，而不是一项高等奖赏。

abstract.en: The word never praises; it only says the thing may be taken.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不称赞，它只说这件东西可以收下。

examples.en: The room was small but perfectly acceptable for one night.
examples.cn: 房间不大，但住一晚完全过得去。

examples.en: We need a solution that is acceptable to both sides.
examples.cn: 我们需要一个双方都能接受的方案。

examples.en: Leaving early is acceptable if you tell the office first.
examples.cn: 只要事先跟办公室说一声，早退是可以的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞普特伯」——手伸过去把东西接住，点头收下，就是可接受的。

root: 拉丁语 accipere「接受」由 ad-「向」加 capere「拿取」构成；其反复动词 acceptare 产生晚期拉丁语 acceptabilis「可接受的」，再经古法语 acceptable 进入英语。更早的词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Acceptable always describes something held out for approval: a quality, a deal, a behaviour, a rule, a burden, a gift, a sentence, or a document.
sensesIntro.cn: acceptable 始终描述某样被递出来等待认可的东西：质量、交易、行为、规则、负担、礼物、句子或证件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holds something out, and the other side nods and takes it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西递出来，另一方点头接住。

branches.en: QUALITY: what meets the minimum standard is taken in, though nobody praises it.
branches.cn: 质量线：达到最低标准的东西被收下，虽然没人称赞它。

branches.en: CONSENT: a deal both sides take, and a gift a god receives gladly.
branches.cn: 同意线：双方都接下的交易，以及神明欣然收下的供品。

branches.en: RULES: society and authority decide what may be taken in.
branches.cn: 规则线：社会与权威决定什么可以被接纳。

branches.en: ENDURANCE: the body keeps taking what it cannot push away.
branches.cn: 忍受线：身体持续接纳它推不开的东西。

branches.en: VALIDITY: grammar and offices check whether the thing may pass.
branches.cn: 有效线：语法与办事机构查验这样东西能否通过。

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle-based root plus an ordinary English adjective suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语分词词根加上普通的英语形容词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin accipere, acceptare and acceptabilis are recorded; only the oldest root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accipere、acceptare 与 acceptabilis 均有记录，只有最早的词根属于重构形式。

items.exampleCN: capere 是表示「拿取」的词根。

items.example: The variant appears in accept and reception.
items.exampleCN: 这个变体出现在 accept 与 reception 中。

definition_zh: 联邦的；联邦政府的；联邦制的
definition_en: relating to a union of states, to a central government, or to the system that joins them
core_image: 首都的议会大厅里，各州代表围坐一圈，桌上摊着同一份法律草案
scene: 各州代表在首都开会，商量全国统一的法律。 Federal law applies across all states.
sceneCN: 这里 federal 是「联邦的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：联邦法律适用于所有州。

senses.title: Relating to a union of states
senses.definition: relating to a union of states under one central authority
senses.definitionCN: 与在一个中央权威下联合的各州有关
senses.example: Federal law sets the minimum age.
senses.exampleCN: 联邦法律规定了最低年龄。
senses.why: This is the core political sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的政治义。

senses.title: Of the central government
senses.definition: belonging to the central government rather than a state
senses.definitionCN: 属于中央政府而非州政府的
senses.example: The federal government funds the program.
senses.exampleCN: 联邦政府为这个项目提供资金。
senses.why: In a federation, the central level is called federal.
senses.whyCN: 在联邦制中，中央层面被称为联邦的。

senses.title: Of the federal system
senses.definition: relating to the system that shares power between states and center
senses.definitionCN: 与在州和中央之间分配权力的制度有关
senses.example: They debated the federal system for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们就联邦制度辩论了数小时。
senses.why: The adjective also names the system itself.
senses.whyCN: 该形容词也直接指称整套制度。

intro.en: Federal comes from Latin foedus, a treaty or league, through the adjective foederalis.
intro.cn: federal 源自拉丁语 foedus（条约、联盟），经形容词 foederalis 传入。

items.en: Foedus meant a treaty or alliance.
items.cn: foedus 意为条约或联盟。

items.en: Foederalis meant belonging to a treaty or league.
items.cn: foederalis 意为属于条约或联盟的。

items.en: Fédéral carried the political sense into French.
items.cn: fédéral 把这一政治义带入法语。

items.en: Federal entered English to describe leagues of states.
items.cn: federal 以「州际联盟」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word became central to the government of the United States.
items.cn: 该词成为美国政府体制的核心用语。

note.en: Federal is compared with similar-looking words and with words for national government.
note.cn: 把 federal 与形近词以及表示国家政府的词作比较。

entries.definition: a ceremony for someone who has died
entries.definitionCN: 葬礼

entries.definition: relating to land and service in the Middle Ages
entries.definitionCN: 封建的

entries.definition: based on facts
entries.definitionCN: 事实的

entries.definition: relating to a whole country
entries.definitionCN: 国家的

entries.definition: at the middle or main point
entries.definitionCN: 中央的

entries.definition: a group of states joined together
entries.definitionCN: 联盟；联邦

normalIntro.en: Federal points to the joined states and their shared central government.
normalIntro.cn: federal 指向联合的各州及其共同的中央政府。

normal.en: Federal law applies across state borders.
normal.cn: 联邦法律跨州界适用。

normal.en: Federal and state powers are often divided.
normal.cn: 联邦权力与州权力常常分开。

normal.en: A federation is the union itself.
normal.cn: federation 就是联合体本身。

normal.en: Federalism is the principle behind the split of power.
normal.cn: federalism 是权力分配背后的原则。

normal.en: Federal and feudal look alike but have different roots.
normal.cn: federal 与 feudal 形近，但词源不同。

abstract.en: A federation joins many states without erasing them.
abstract.cn: 联邦把许多州联合起来，却不抹去它们。

abstract.en: Shared law needs a shared center.
abstract.cn: 共同的法律需要一个共同的中央。

abstract.en: The word began with a treaty and grew into a government.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一份条约开始，成长为一种政府形态。

examples.en: Federal law sets the minimum age.
examples.cn: 联邦法律规定了最低年龄。

examples.en: The federal government funds the program.
examples.cn: 联邦政府为这个项目提供资金。

examples.en: They debated the federal system for hours.
examples.cn: 他们就联邦制度辩论了数小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: federal 源自拉丁语 foedus（条约、联盟），核心是「通过条约联合起来的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 foedus（条约、联盟），经 foederalis，核心义「依条约联合的各州及其中央」。

sensesIntro.en: Federal means relating to a union of states, its central government, or its system of shared power.
sensesIntro.cn: federal 意为与各州联合有关、属于联邦政府，或属于联邦制度。

core.en: A shared center that holds separate states together.
core.cn: 把各个州维系在一起的共同中央。

branches.en: Belonging to the union of states.
branches.cn: 属于各州联合体。

branches.en: Belonging to the central government.
branches.cn: 属于中央政府。

branches.en: Belonging to the system of shared power.
branches.cn: 属于权力共享的制度。

branches.en: The union and its center are two faces of one structure.
branches.cn: 联合体与其中央是同一结构的两个面。

branches.en: A union of states needs a federal design.
branches.cn: 各州的联合需要联邦式的设计。

intro.en: Federal forms words for the union, its supporters, and its central reach.
intro.cn: federal 构成表示联邦、其支持者与中央范围的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin foedus and foederalis are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 foedus 与 foederalis 是历史词根。

items.meaning: relating to a union of states
items.example: The federal court heard the case.

items.exampleCN: 联邦主义者主张强大的中央。
联邦主义者在辩论中获胜。

items.example: The plan would federalize the service.
items.exampleCN: 该计划将使这项服务联邦化。

items.meaning: a union of states or groups
items.exampleCN: 这个联合会有十个成员。

items.example: A confederal system keeps states stronger.
The confederation lasted only a few years.
